    5.1 Complexes retain the equations and their solutions

    A cochain complex is a sequence of vector spaces and linear maps

    ⋯⟶Vn−1→dVn→dVn+1⟶⋯,d2=0.\cdots\longrightarrow V^{n-1}\xrightarrow{d}V^n \xrightarrow{d}V^{n+1}\longrightarrow\cdots, \qquad d^2=0.

    The superscript is the cohomological degree, and the differential has degree +1+1. A vector killed by dd is a cycle; a vector of the form dwdw is a boundary. Their quotient is

    Hn(V)=ker⁡(d:Vn→Vn+1)/im⁡(d:Vn−1→Vn).H^n(V)=\ker(d:V^n\to V^{n+1})/ \operatorname{im}(d:V^{n-1}\to V^n).

    The distinction between a boundary and a chosen primitive matters. Knowing that v=dwv=dw is solvable does not specify ww, and different choices can enter later operations.

    Our shift convention is

    V[1]n=Vn+1,dV[1]=−dV.V[1]^n=V^{n+1},\qquad d_{V[1]}=-d_V.

    Thus a vector of degree rr in VV has degree r−1r-1 in V[1]V[1]. Write svsv for that shifted vector; ss has degree −1-1. Tensor products use the Koszul sign rule:

    d(v⊗w)=dv⊗w+(−1)|v|v⊗dw,d(v\otimes w)=dv\otimes w+(-1)^{|v|}v\otimes dw,

    where |v||v| denotes the degree of a homogeneous vector.

    A chain map f:V→Wf:V\to W commutes with the differentials. A homotopy from gg to ff is a degree-minus-one map hh satisfying

    f−g=dWh+hdV.f-g=d_Wh+hd_V.

    Homotopic maps induce the same cohomology map, but the homotopy contains information that this induced map forgets. More generally, maps of all degrees form a complex

    Homr⁡(V,W)=∏nHom⁡(Vn,Wn+r),∂f=dWf−(−1)rfdV.\operatorname{Hom}^r(V,W)=\prod_n\operatorname{Hom}(V^n,W^{n+r}), \qquad \partial f=d_Wf-(-1)^rfd_V.

    Chain maps are its degree-zero cycles, and homotopies identify maps whose difference is a boundary. The product over nn is intentional: a degree-rr map has a component on every degree of VV.

    A chain map is a quasi-isomorphism if it induces an isomorphism on every cohomology group. The ordinary derived category formally makes these maps invertible. We will also retain the derived mapping complexes, obtained by resolving the inputs as necessary, rather than keeping only their degree-zero cohomology. This enhanced form of the derived category remembers homotopies and homotopies between them; it is the meaning intended when the geometric theorem below refers to higher mapping spaces.

    Consider the complex

    ℂu1⊕︎ℂu2→ dt ℂv1⊕︎ℂv2,dtu1=tv1,dtu2=0,\mathbb C u_1\oplus\mathbb C u_2 \xrightarrow{\ d_t\ } \mathbb C v_1\oplus\mathbb C v_2, \qquad d_tu_1=tv_1,\quad d_tu_2=0,

    in degrees zero and one. For t≠0t\ne0, the u1,v1u_1,v_1 summand is contractible: set h(v1)=t−1u1h(v_1)=t^{-1}u_1 and let hh vanish on the other basis vectors. If pp projects to the remaining u2,v2u_2,v_2 summand and ii includes it, then

    dh+hd=1−ip.dh+hd=1-ip.

    Both cohomology groups have dimension one. At t=0t=0, both have dimension two. The Euler characteristic is zero throughout, but the contracting homotopy has a pole at the point where the cohomology changes. A fibrewise calculation and a comparison valid over the whole parameter line are therefore different assertions.

    5.2 Relations can leave a higher operation

    A differential graded algebra is a graded associative algebra AA, equipped with a differential satisfying

    d(ab)=(da)b+(−1)|a|adb.d(ab)=(da)b+(-1)^{|a|}a\,db.

    Its cohomology is an associative graded algebra. Passing to cohomology nevertheless loses information about how products become boundaries.

    Here is an explicit example. Let

    A=T(a,b,c,x,y),|a|=|b|=|c|=|x|=|y|=1,A=T(a,b,c,x,y),\qquad |a|=|b|=|c|=|x|=|y|=1,

    be the free associative graded algebra on five generators, with

    da=db=dc=0,dx=ab,dy=bc.da=db=dc=0,\qquad dx=ab,\qquad dy=bc.

    Extend dd by the graded Leibniz rule. Since a,b,ca,b,c are closed, d2=0d^2=0. The cohomology products [a][b][a][b] and [b][c][b][c] vanish. The chosen primitives x,yx,y then give

    z=ay+xc,dz=−abc+abc=0.z=ay+xc, \qquad dz=-abc+abc=0.

    This cycle is not a boundary: the degree-two boundaries are spanned by abab and bcbc, whereas ay+xcay+xc is a different linear combination of words in the free algebra.

    Changing xx or yy by a degree-one cycle changes [z][z] by an element of [a]H1(A)+H1(A)[c][a]H^1(A)+H^1(A)[c]. In this example H1(A)H^1(A) is spanned by [a],[b],[c][a],[b],[c], and that indeterminacy cannot remove the words ayay and xcxc. The resulting nonzero coset is a triple Massey product: a higher operation defined from two vanishing products and choices of their primitives. The multiplication table on cohomology records the two zero products but does not determine this further class.

    The same issue arises when an associative multiplication is transferred to a smaller complex. Suppose maps i:H→Ai:H\to A, p:A→Hp:A\to H and a homotopy hh satisfy pi=1pi=1 and dh+hd=1−ipdh+hd=1-ip. Projecting the product gives pμ(i⊗i)p\mu(i\otimes i) on HH. Composing products introduces the intermediate projection ipip; replacing it by the identity produces terms containing hh. Those terms are the first higher operations. A comparison that retains only the projected binary product can discard the very primitives needed to compose it.

    5.3 Words and the reduced bar construction

    An augmentation of a unital dg algebra is a dg algebra map ϵ:A→k\epsilon:A\to k, where kk is the ground field. It splits the underlying complex as A=k⋅1⊕︎A‾A=k\cdot1\oplus\bar A, with A‾=ker⁡ϵ\bar A=\ker\epsilon. The reduced bar construction, including its empty word, is

    BA=Tc(A‾[1])=k⊕︎⨁n≥1(A‾[1])⊗n.BA=T^c(\bar A[1]) =k\oplus\bigoplus_{n\ge1}(\bar A[1])^{\otimes n}.

    We write

    [a1|⋯|an]=sa1⊗⋯⊗san,|[a1|⋯|an]|=∑i|ai|−n.[a_1|\cdots|a_n]=sa_1\otimes\cdots\otimes sa_n, \qquad |[a_1|\cdots|a_n]|=\sum_i|a_i|-n.

    The superscript cc indicates the tensor coalgebra. Its coproduct splits a word at every position:

    Δ[a1|⋯|an]=∑i=0n[a1|⋯|ai]⊗[ai+1|⋯|an].\Delta[a_1|\cdots|a_n] =\sum_{i=0}^n[a_1|\cdots|a_i] \otimes[a_{i+1}|\cdots|a_n].

    The empty word is 11. This deconcatenation is coassociative because splitting at two positions gives the same three consecutive subwords in either order.

    The bar differential has two kinds of terms. It applies the differential of AA to one letter, or multiplies two adjacent letters. With our cohomological suspension convention, its defining components are

    b1(sa)=−s(da),b2(sa⊗sb)=(−1)|a|s(ab).b_1(sa)=-s(da),\qquad b_2(sa\otimes sb)=(-1)^{|a|}s(ab).

    They extend to words by applying the operation in each possible position. Passing a degree-one operation across a prefix contributes the degree of that prefix. Explicitly,

    b[a1|⋯|an]=∑i=1n(−1)1+∑j<i(|aj|−1)[a1|⋯|dai|⋯|an]+∑i=1n−1(−1)|ai|+∑j<i(|aj|−1)[a1|⋯|aiai+1|⋯|an].\begin{aligned} b[a_1|\cdots|a_n] ={}&\sum_{i=1}^n (-1)^{1+\sum_{j<i}(|a_j|-1)} [a_1|\cdots|da_i|\cdots|a_n]\\ &+\sum_{i=1}^{n-1} (-1)^{|a_i|+\sum_{j<i}(|a_j|-1)} [a_1|\cdots|a_ia_{i+1}|\cdots|a_n]. \end{aligned}

    The equation b2=0b^2=0 expresses three familiar facts: d2=0d^2=0, the Leibniz rule, and associativity. For an ordinary algebra concentrated in degree zero, the internal-differential terms vanish, and

    b[a|b]=[ab],b[a|b|c]=[ab|c]−[a|bc].b[a|b]=[ab],\qquad b[a|b|c]=[ab|c]-[a|bc].

    Applying bb again gives [(ab)c]−[a(bc)]=0[(ab)c]-[a(bc)]=0. The length-three word makes the relation between the two multiplications into an explicit boundary equation. Longer words organize the compatible ways of repeating this operation. These are the usual algebraic bar formulas, expressed in cohomological degrees; see Loday–Vallette, Algebraic Operads, §§2.2–2.3.

    Two small algebras show what this complex measures. For A=k[x]A=k[x], augmented by x↦0x\mapsto0, the two-term free resolution

    0⟶A→xA⟶k⟶00\longrightarrow A\xrightarrow{\,x\,}A\longrightarrow k\longrightarrow0

    computes the same groups as the bar resolution. Tensoring over AA with kk kills its differential, so

    H∗(BA)=k⊕︎k⋅[x],|[x]|=−1.H^*(BA)=k\oplus k\cdot[x],\qquad |[x]|=-1.

    In the bar complex itself, [x2]=b[x|x][x^2]=b[x|x], and similarly higher powers in a single letter do not give new degree-minus-one classes.

    For A=k[ϵ]/(ϵ2)A=k[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2), the augmentation ideal is one-dimensional and its product is zero. Every bar differential is therefore zero:

    BA=⨁n≥0k[ϵ|⋯|ϵ],H−n(BA)=k(n≥0).BA=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}k[\epsilon|\cdots|\epsilon], \qquad H^{-n}(BA)=k\quad(n\ge0).

    The corresponding free resolution has multiplication by ϵ\epsilon at every step. It is exact before tensoring with kk, and every differential becomes zero afterwards. Thus the single relation ϵ2=0\epsilon^2=0 produces homological information in arbitrarily long words. These groups are traditionally denoted TornA⁡(k,k)\operatorname{Tor}_n^A(k,k), with n=−cohomological degreen=-\text{cohomological degree}.

    5.4 One differential encodes all associativity homotopies

    The word complex also accommodates multiplication that is associative only through specified homotopies. A degree-one map bb on Tc(V[1])T^c(V[1]) is a coderivation if

    Δb=(b⊗1+1⊗b)Δ,\Delta b=(b\otimes1+1\otimes b)\Delta,

    with the graded tensor convention. Such a map is determined by its components

    bn:(V[1])⊗n⟶V[1].b_n:(V[1])^{\otimes n}\longrightarrow V[1].

    On a finite word only finitely many components can act. An uncurved A∞A_\infty-algebra structure is a coderivation with no constant component and with b2=0b^2=0. Undoing the shifts gives operations mn:V⊗n→Vm_n:V^{\otimes n}\to V of degree 2−n2-n. The suspended formulation fixes the signs without a separate convention for every arity.

    The length-one equation is m12=0m_1^2=0; length two says that m2m_2 is a chain map. At length three, the associator of m2m_2 is the boundary of a degree-minus-one operation. At length four, the homotopies along the five parenthesizations of a fourfold product form a closed compatibility expression, and the next operation supplies its primitive. Continuing gives all the equations at once. Equivalently, their suspended form is

    ∑r+s+t=nbr+1+t(1⊗r⊗bs⊗1⊗t)=0,\sum_{r+s+t=n} b_{r+1+t}(1^{\otimes r}\otimes b_s\otimes1^{\otimes t})=0,

    where composition of graded tensor maps supplies the signs.

    This is the meaning of coherence here: the actual operations and these compatibility equations are included in the structure. An associative product on cohomology does not provide them. Nor do a binary operation and one ternary homotopy determine all higher operations. The bar complex provides a place to write the entire family, while finite words ensure that its differential is an actual algebraic operation.

    5.5 Cobar reverses the construction

    Let C=k⊕︎C‾C=k\oplus\bar C be a coaugmented dg coalgebra. Its reduced coproduct is Δ‾:C‾→C‾⊗C‾\bar\Delta:\bar C\to\bar C\otimes\bar C, obtained by removing the two terms involving 11. The coalgebra is conilpotent if sufficiently many iterated reduced coproducts kill each element. The tensor coalgebra above has this property because a word cannot be split into more nonempty pieces than its length.

    The cobar construction is the tensor algebra

    ΩC=T(C‾[−1]).\Omega C=T(\bar C[-1]).

    Write ucuc for a generator in C‾[−1]\bar C[-1], so |uc|=|c|+1|uc|=|c|+1. If Δ‾c=∑c′⊗c′′\bar\Delta c=\sum c'\otimes c'', its differential is the derivation determined by

    dΩ(uc)=−u(dCc)+∑(−1)|c′|+1(uc′)(uc′′).d_\Omega(uc)=-u(d_Cc) +\sum(-1)^{|c'|+1}(uc')(uc'').

    Thus bar shortens words by multiplication, while cobar lengthens them by coproduct. The signs are compatible: when a,ba,b have degree zero, the generator u[a|b]u[a|b] in ΩBA\Omega BA satisfies

    dΩu[a|b]=−u[ab]+(u[a])(u[b]).d_\Omega u[a|b]=-u[ab]+(u[a])(u[b]).

    The map ΩBA→A\Omega BA\to A sending u[a]u[a] to aa and the longer single generators to zero respects this equation. Its extra generators explicitly encode the multiplication relations in AA.

    More generally, a degree-one map τ:C→A\tau:C\to A, vanishing on the coaugmentation and landing in A‾\bar A, is a twisting cochain when

    dAτ+τdC+μA(τ⊗τ)Δ‾=0.d_A\tau+\tau d_C+\mu_A(\tau\otimes\tau)\bar\Delta=0.

    Here (τ⊗τ)(c′⊗c′′)=(−1)|c′|τ(c′)⊗τ(c′′)(\tau\otimes\tau)(c'\otimes c'')=(-1)^{|c'|}\tau(c')\otimes\tau(c''). This one equation says exactly that uc↦τ(c)uc\mapsto\tau(c) extends to a dg algebra map ΩC→A\Omega C\to A. For conilpotent CC, iterating its reduced coproduct gives the corresponding dg coalgebra map C→BAC\to BA. We obtain the strict bar–cobar adjunction

    HomdgAlg⁡(ΩC,A)≅Tw⁡(C,A)≅HomdgCoalg⁡(C,BA).\operatorname{Hom}_{\rm dgAlg}(\Omega C,A) \cong\operatorname{Tw}(C,A) \cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\rm dgCoalg}(C,BA).

    An adjunction provides comparison maps. Whether those maps are equivalences requires a theorem about the objects and weak equivalences under consideration. The geometry of ordered configurations supplies an especially useful finiteness condition for such a theorem.

    5.6 Ordered cuts give a finite geometric bar construction

    Let XX be a smooth separated finite-type curve over a characteristic-zero field kk. Write 𝒟(Xn)\mathcal D(X^n) for the unbounded derived category of right algebraic differential modules with quasi-coherent underlying modules, retaining its higher mapping spaces. A word coefficient system consists of complexes Mn∈𝒟(Xn)M_n\in\mathcal D(X^n) for n≥1n\ge1, together with coherent equivalences

    dα!Mn≃Mm(α:[n]↠[m] monotone),d_\alpha^!M_n\simeq M_m \qquad \bigl(\alpha:[n]\twoheadrightarrow[m]\text{ monotone}\bigr),

    where dα(x)i=xα(i)d_\alpha(x)_i=x_{\alpha(i)}. Here dα!d_\alpha^! is extraordinary derived pullback. The equivalences include their compatibilities under composition and all higher homotopies. Add an isolated empty coefficient M0∈D(k)M_0\in D(k), with no collision arrow from a nonempty configuration to it. Denote this category by 𝒲X\mathcal W_X; the integer nn is the arity.

    For p+q=np+q=n, let Up,q⊂XnU_{p,q}\subset X^n be the open set on which every point in the first block is distinct from every point in the second. There is no separation condition within either block. With jp,q:Up,q↪Xnj_{p,q}:U_{p,q}\hookrightarrow X^n, define consecutive-cut convolution by

    (M⋆N)n=⨁p+q=nRjp,q∗jp,q∗(Mp⊠𝐋Nq).(M\star N)_n= \bigoplus_{p+q=n}Rj_{p,q*}j_{p,q}^* (M_p\boxtimes^{\mathbf L}N_q).

    The symbol ⊠𝐋\boxtimes^{\mathbf L} means derived external tensor product. Open direct image allows the prescribed singular behaviour along the removed diagonals; it is not a choice of a finite pole bound. Empty blocks contribute their complexes over kk. Iterated products use consecutive blocks in their written order. Localizing at their interblock diagonals gives the common domain for every parenthesization.

    The unit is 𝟏=(k,0,0,…)\mathbf1=(k,0,0,\ldots). An augmented algebra is connected in arity if its augmentation identifies A0A_0 with kk; a counital coaugmented coalgebra has the analogous condition C0≃kC_0\simeq k. This says nothing about cohomological degrees. The positive-arity summands A‾,C‾\bar A,\bar C have the decisive property

    (M1⋆⋯⋆Mr)n=0if all M0i=0 and r>n.(M^1\star\cdots\star M^r)_n=0 \quad\text{if all }M^i_0=0\text{ and }r>n.

    Indeed, every nonzero term assigns at least one point to each of the rr factors.

    Theorem: connected consecutive-cut duality. In 𝒲X\mathcal W_X, bar and cobar for consecutive-cut convolution are inverse equivalences between connected augmented coherent associative algebras and connected counital coaugmented coherent coassociative coalgebras. The equivalence includes their full mapping spaces. It requires no cohomological boundedness or finite-dimensionality of coefficients.

    “Coherent” means that all higher associativity or coassociativity comparisons are retained, not just the equations visible on cohomology. One can compute the equivalence with strict dg representatives. Its proof uses the arity filtration: the normalized bar and cobar layers are

    A‾⋆r[r],C‾⋆r[−r].\bar A^{\star r}[r],\qquad \bar C^{\star r}[-r].

    In arity nn, they vanish for r>nr>n. Consequently the relevant constructions stabilize after finitely many normalized stages in each coefficient. No interchange of an arbitrary infinite tensor product with an inverse limit is needed. The underlying filtered associative duality is developed by Matsuoka, Koszul duality between EnE_n-algebras and coalgebras in a filtered category, Lemmas 4.13 and 4.17 (arXiv:1409.6943v4); intrinsic bar and cobar are treated in Lurie, Higher Algebra, §5.2.2.

    One can see the inverse explicitly. Flatten a word of words into rr positive letters. Each of its r−1r-1 internal boundaries may lie inside one word or separate two words. At fixed letters, the part of the differential that changes one such choice gives the augmented cube on those boundaries. For r=2r=2 it is one identity map between two copies of the same coefficient. For r>1r>1, contracting in the first boundary pairs all terms with opposite incidence signs. Only the empty and single-letter contributions survive. The arity bound makes passage from this associated graded calculation to the original object finite at each configuration.

    There are two adjunction conventions to distinguish. The strict twisting-cochain construction above has Ωdg⊣Bdg\Omega_{\rm dg}\dashv B_{\rm dg}. The intrinsic connected equivalence also has the adjunction B⊣ΩB\dashv\Omega, with maps A→ΩBAA\to\Omega BA and BΩC→CB\Omega C\to C. The comparison of the two presentations identifies their equivalences, not their oppositely directed canonical chain maps.

    5.7 The support remembers which cuts were allowed

    A coalgebra CC is factorizing across consecutive cuts if, on every Up,n−pU_{p,n-p}, its cut coproduct

    Cn|Up,n−p⟶(Cp⊠𝐋Cn−p)|Up,n−pC_n|_{U_{p,n-p}}\longrightarrow (C_p\boxtimes^{\mathbf L}C_{n-p})|_{U_{p,n-p}}

    is an equivalence. An associative chiral algebra in the word category is an augmented E1E_1-algebra AA for consecutive-cut convolution, with A0≃kA_0\simeq k, whose bar coalgebra BABA factorizes in this sense. Here E1E_1 means that the multiplication and all its associativity homotopies are retained. Its augmentation ideal has zero empty coefficient. The support theorem below identifies these algebras by the support of their positive-arity coefficients. Put

    Zn=Xn∖⋃p=1n−1Up,n−p,Z1=X.Z_n=X^n\setminus\bigcup_{p=1}^{n-1}U_{p,n-p}, \qquad Z_1=X.

    For a complex FF, derived sections supported on ZZ, denoted RΓZFR\Gamma_ZF, form the fibre of the restriction map F→Rj∗j∗FF\to Rj_*j^*F to the complementary open set.

    Support theorem. Consecutive-cut duality restricts to an equivalence between factorizing coalgebras and connected algebras whose positive-arity coefficients vanish on every cut open. For a factorizing coalgebra,

    ΩCn≃RΓZn(Cn)[−1].\overline{\Omega C}_n\simeq R\Gamma_{Z_n}(C_n)[-1].

    The shift is part of the formula. To see its origin, index a cube by subsets of the n−1n-1 possible cuts. A subset of size r−1r-1 gives rr blocks, hence a cobar term shifted by [−r][-r]. The corresponding localization cube has shift [−(r−1)][-(r-1)]; the two totalizations differ by [−1][-1]. Factorization identifies the entire cut cube with the localization cube, including its maps.

    For three points,

    Z3=(Δ12∪Δ13)∩(Δ13∪Δ23)=Δ13.Z_3=(\Delta_{12}\cup\Delta_{13}) \cap(\Delta_{13}\cup\Delta_{23})=\Delta_{13}.

    Here Δij\Delta_{ij} is the diagonal xi=xjx_i=x_j. A configuration with x1=x3x_1=x_3 and x2x_2 elsewhere defeats both consecutive cuts. The support is therefore larger than the small diagonal where all three points coincide.

    The supported complex alone does not specify the associative algebra. The multiplication on the cut cobar also uses the inverse factorization maps on the separating opens. Its unit lies at the empty configuration. A vacuum marking is separate singleton data: an identification A{1}≅ωX⊗𝒪XGA_{\{1\}}\cong\omega_X\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}G with a left differential module GG and a horizontal map 𝒪X→G\mathcal O_X\to G. A vacuum framing further compares the configuration operations with the simultaneous field products, preserving substitutions, translation and the vacuum.

    The same definition of an associative chiral algebra can be used with the symmetric convolution on the full ordered collision atlas. There, factorization requires each specified coproduct component to be an equivalence. Its support consequence differs from the cut theorem. If C=BAC=BA and UU is the two-point distinct locus, put V=(C{1}⊠C{1})|UV=(C_{\{1\}}\boxtimes C_{\{1\}})|_U. Componentwise factorization gives

    A{1,2}|U≃V[−2].\overline A_{\{1,2\}}|_U\simeq V[-2].

    Thus nonzero VV gives a nonzero coefficient away from the diagonal. Small-diagonal support on the atlas is instead characterized by a joint word-factorization condition, which compares the full direct sum of ordered word terms. It cannot be substituted for the componentwise condition defining the factorizing bar.

    Two different units occur already on these coefficients. For convolution the coaugmentation is a map from kk at the empty configuration. For the coefficientwise extraordinary tensor the unit has nn-point coefficient ωXn[n]\omega_{X^n}[n] on a curve. A map from this second system to a coalgebra, with its compatible insertions, specifies what happens when a vacuum occupies a position. For the current JJ at scalar level k0≠0k_0\ne0, the first product satisfies J(1)J=k0𝟏J_{(1)}J=k_0\mathbf1. A unital map of field algebras to the scalar field algebra would send its left side to zero and its right side to k0k_0. Projection to the vacuum coefficient is a linear functional. Preservation of field products is a stronger condition that fails on this pair.

    On the affine line there is a field recognition theorem for the normalized degree-zero coefficient systems on the full Ran space. Its geometric data include the supported binary lattice with its principal-part map, coherent collision maps in every arity, a nonzero vacuum with insertion and retraction along collisions, and translation. In a coordinate zz, the translation derivation DD is locally nilpotent on the unary sections, differentiates scalar functions, commutes with the constant vector-field action, kills the vacuum and preserves the separated lattices under simultaneous translation. The reconstructed state space is ker⁡D\ker D. Multiplying by powers of a difference before taking principal parts recovers every coefficient of the field, and comparison of the two orders recovers its exchange. This gives an equivalence with the corresponding quantum vertex algebras over the field, with invertible exchange finite Laurent on each input in both directions. Extension of morphisms between such objects uses the binary lattice, residue and exchange. Existence of all their collision data is a separate hypothesis. For example, on the cut family with state algebra k[ϵ]/(ϵ2)k[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2) and translation zero, the ternary pole lattice at 13|213|2 forces a putative exchange to act on ϵ⊗ϵ\epsilon\otimes\epsilon by the cut parameter c∈k×c\in k^\times or its inverse, according to the direction of crossing. Unitarity then forces c2=1c^2=1. Both signs extend. The other cut objects still have their local vacuum.

    One can also transpose the geometric bar. For bounded holonomic coefficients, Verdier duality sends the cut coproduct with j∗j_*-extension to multiplication with j!j_!-extension, and sends extraordinary collision pullbacks to ordinary ones. It therefore produces an algebra in the category with the dual transition maps. A pointwise cochain dual paired with the occupied vacuum instead has multiplication formed with j∗j_*. The comparison between those open extensions has the normal links calculated in Chapter 4 when its own open and coefficients agree with that fully distinct Betti problem. The input of a word cut can allow collisions inside each block. Its comparison requires the link for that open.

    5.8 Rational exchange on all finite collision diagrams

    To see what extra information a full diagram supplies, work over a commutative algebra RR over a characteristic-zero field kk. Let UU be the affine line with finitely many kk-rational punctures removed. Take a flat state module VV over RR, a free vacuum summand, translation TT and lower-truncated fields Y(a,u)bY(a,u)b with vacuum, translation and weak associativity. Suppose its exchange 𝒮(z)\mathcal S(z) and its inverse are finite Laurent expressions on each state tensor. They fix the vacuum slots and satisfy the translation, unitarity, Yang–Baxter, field locality and exchange hexagon identities. The hexagon says how to move a spectator past a product of two fields. These are identities over RR, including when RR has nilpotents.

    Assign a coordinate zBz_B to every block BB of a partition of a finite label set II. On the locus of distinct block positions take the external field coefficients, invert the differences of block coordinates, and push forward along the partition diagonal, retaining every finite derivative of its delta section. These are the Cousin coefficients. In their cobar complex, a word groups the blocks into successive nonempty factors. The differential splits one factor or merges two blocks inside it. Put Xab=𝒮ba(zb−za)X_{ab}=\mathcal S_{ba}(z_b-z_a) on fixed labelled slots. For an unsplit two-block factor with coefficient xx, its boundary in the two possible orders and the merged support is

    x[a][b]−(Xabx)[b][a]−(rab∘x)[m].x[a][b]-(X_{ab}x)[b][a]-(r^\circ_{ab}x)[m] .

    Here rab∘r^\circ_{ab} takes the whole polar part of the multiplier times Y(a,za−zb)bY(a,z_a-z_b)b, expanding every spectator at the surviving root mm. For instance a multiplier 1/(d+u)1/(d+u), with dd a nonzero spectator difference and uu the collision coordinate, turns a double pole into

    1u2(d+u)=1du2−1d2u+O(1).\frac{1}{u^2(d+u)}=\frac{1}{d\,u^2}-\frac{1}{d^2u}+O(1).

    Thus a spectator can change the simple residue. Changing the surviving root transfers the entire normal distribution with its orientation.

    The Spencer complex adjoins an exterior tangent vector eie_i of degree −1-1 at each label. Its differential contracts tangent factors with the covariant derivatives, which on the block coefficient are ∇B=∂zB+TB\nabla_B=\partial_{z_B}+T_B. Denote by K(I)K(I) the total complex including the word differential. A surjection α:I↠J\alpha:I\twoheadrightarrow J gives a map K(J)→K(I)K(J)\to K(I). It inserts the supported coefficient on the repeated labels and sends

    ej⟼∑α(i)=jei.e_j\longmapsto\sum_{\alpha(i)=j}e_i .

    Ordering the quotient labels by their largest preimages determines which adjacent exchanges to apply inside each word factor. Taking a maximum in two stages agrees with taking it once. Unitarity and Yang–Baxter identify different presentations of the same order change. The exchange hexagon and the re-rooting identity for the full principal part make these transitions chain maps. Concatenation of two words, followed by localization at all differences between their blocks, gives an associative external multiplication compatible with the support maps. The empty set carries its own scalar RR.

    For the interlaced partition 13|2413|24, first multiply at the two block positions and then repeat each position. On the exterior tangent ea∧ebe_a\wedge e_b this gives

    (e1+e3)∧(e2+e4).(e_1+e_3)\wedge(e_2+e_4).

    Doing the two repetitions first and multiplying the results produces the same wedge, including the sign of e3∧e2e_3\wedge e_2. The coefficients have the same property on normal derivatives. Write u=z1−z3, h=z2−z4, d=z3−z4u=z_1-z_3,\ h=z_2-z_4,\ d=z_3-z_4, so the cross difference is d+u−hd+u-h. On the product of principal parts [u−2][h−2][u^{-2}][h^{-2}], u2u^2 and h2h^2 act by zero. Expanding 1/(d+u−h)1/(d+u-h) leaves a mixed term −2d−3[u−1][h−1]-2d^{-3}[u^{-1}][h^{-1}]. Localizing first and expanding at the joint support gives the same value as expanding on the two factors. In general every fixed total normal order truncates this calculation.

    Exchange itself can be detected over the original ring. Take the polynomial current JJ with Wick contraction P(d)=κd−2+λd−1P(d)=\kappa d^{-2}+\lambda d^{-1} over k[κ,λ]k[\kappa,\lambda]. On the primary oscillator polynomials the order change is the finite exponential of (2λ/d)∂J⊗∂J(2\lambda/d)\partial_J\otimes\partial_J, with d=za−zbd=z_a-z_b. In particular

    Xab(J2⊗J2)=J2⊗J2+8λdJ⊗J+8λ2d2𝟏⊗𝟏.X_{ab}(J^2\otimes J^2)=J^2\otimes J^2+ \frac{8\lambda}{d}J\otimes J+ \frac{8\lambda^2}{d^2}\mathbf1\otimes\mathbf1 .

    Identifying labels 1 and 3 while 2 stays separate changes the root order on the two-block factor. Crossing before the identification or using the induced order afterwards gives this same operator, together with the orientation sign on the factor. At κ=0,λ=ϵ\kappa=0,\lambda=\epsilon, ϵ2=0\epsilon^2=0, its first correction survives. Specialization to the residue field would erase exactly the order change being tested.

    Theorem (the algebraic collision integral). Form GU(V)G_U(V) by taking an algebraic direct sum over chains of surjections, placing a chain of length pp in simplicial degree −p-p, with the usual alternating face maps on the K(I)K(I). Shuffling two chains and concatenating their coefficient words makes GU(V)G_U(V) a unital dg algebra over RR. Its degree-zero cohomology is the intrinsic all-arity mode algebra 𝖬U(V)\mathsf M_U(V).

    Here 𝖬U(V)\mathsf M_U(V) is the quotient of the rational multipoint fields by translation derivatives and the relations x−σix−ρixx-\sigma_i x-\rho_i x with arbitrary spectators. The operator σi\sigma_i exchanges and relabels two neighbouring inputs, and ρi\rho_i takes the supported simple residue after the full Taylor transfer. The equality in degree zero comes from a chain map. Insert a configuration cochain as a word of singleton factors by ϕ\phi, and let σˆi,ρˆi\widehat\sigma_i,\widehat\rho_i act also on the exterior tangents. For each adjacent pair there is a degree-minus-one homotopy

    dhi+hid=ϕ(1−σˆi−ρˆi).dh_i+h_id=\phi(1-\widehat\sigma_i-\widehat\rho_i).

    The unsplit double factor supplies the three terms of the word boundary above. A normal contraction replaces its full polar part by the pushed-forward simple residue, and the transposition and collision edges of the surjection diagram cancel the differences of representatives. Conversely every boundary in degree zero comes from one tangent, one double factor or one diagram edge. Listing the surviving blocks in word order therefore gives the inverse on the stated quotient. This argument works on all spectator coefficients and on the whole Spencer complex.

    The filtration by the number of labels also determines the additive complex. Write

    𝒟r=𝒪(Confr⁡U)⊗kV⊗Rr⊗RΛ∙Rr\mathcal D_r=\mathcal O(\operatorname{Conf}_r U)\otimes_k V^{\otimes_R r}\otimes_R\Lambda^\bullet R^r

    with its Spencer differential and the exchange action of Σr\Sigma_r, including its permutation of tangents. In cardinality rr, all proper collision partitions already enter from a smaller set. On the discrete partition the complex of orders and their consecutive groupings is the cellular complex of a permutohedron, a contractible polytope whose vertices are the orders. The resulting layer is (𝒟r)Σr(\mathcal D_r)_{\Sigma_r}, the coinvariants for the indicated exchange action. In characteristic zero the Eulerian idempotents on words, the projections to symmetric powers of primitive letters for the auxiliary unshuffle coproduct, split these layers additively:

    GU(V)≃R⊕︎⨁r≥1(𝒟r)Σras complexes.G_U(V)\simeq R\oplus\bigoplus_{r\ge1}(\mathcal D_r)_{\Sigma_r} \qquad\text{as complexes}.

    Each projector has a single possibly nonzero layer, so the cardinality spectral sequence degenerates on its first page. Multiplication in GU(V)G_U(V) retains the lower-cardinality residue terms. The relation homotopies identify degree zero, while a comparison in negative degrees with an independent derived algebra of modes or a global geometric pushforward requires its own map. Chapter 13 relates integration to the reconstruction of field coefficients.

    An integral of configuration coefficients gives an algebra. To reconstruct representations from it one must determine which modules it sees. The unit and counit of the relevant adjunction give that test in the next chapter.

    Previous4 Factorization and collision geometryNext6 Derived adjunctions and inductionDerived tensor and Hom come with an actual unit map. At nonrational shifted affine level, under the smooth realization hypotheses, that unit recovers every unbounded source module. At other levels a telescope tests what can disappear.

    Part II Duality and centresChapter 6 of 18

    6

    Derived adjunctions and induction

    A representation can be studied through the maps into it from a chosen module WW. These maps carry an action of the endomorphisms of WW, and tensoring them back with WW gives a candidate reconstruction. The question is whether

    W⊗B𝐋RHom⁡(W,M)⟶MW\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}\operatorname{RHom}(W,M)\longrightarrow M

    recovers the original representation, where BB is the appropriate derived endomorphism algebra with its opposite multiplication. The arrow matters: an isomorphism between the two objects would not by itself identify this reconstruction map.

    For affine currents the choice of WW is decisive. Its lowest-energy subspace is the entire regular representation of the horizontal Lie algebra. When the shifted affine level lies outside ℚ\mathbb Q, this choice yields a reconstruction theorem for every simple complex Lie algebra, under the smooth realization hypotheses below. If there are DD positive roots, then a tensor of DD positive-weight augmentation factors survives and every such tensor of D+1D+1 factors vanishes. The resulting finite filtration works even for unbounded complexes. At rational shift one can construct positive-weight words of any finite length. Determining what affine realization sees there requires the adjunction itself.

    6.1 What the unit and counit measure

    For a differential graded (dg) algebra BB, the ordinary derived category D(B)D(B) is obtained from complexes of BB-modules by inverting quasi-isomorphisms. We retain its enhancement, so derived mapping complexes and their composition remain available. There is no bound on cohomological degrees. As before, differentials raise degree by one and L[1]n=Ln+1L[1]^n=L^{n+1}.

    Let AA be another dg algebra and let WW be an AA-BB bimodule. Derived tensor and derived Hom give an adjunction

    Φ=W⊗B𝐋−:D(B)⇄D(A):Ψ=RHomA⁡(W,−).\Phi=W\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}-:D(B) \rightleftarrows D(A): \Psi=\operatorname{RHom}_A(W,-).

    Its defining property is the natural equivalence

    RHomA⁡(ΦL,M)≃RHomB⁡(L,ΨM).\operatorname{RHom}_A(\Phi L,M) \simeq\operatorname{RHom}_B(L,\Psi M).

    The unit ηL:L→ΨΦL\eta_L:L\to\Psi\Phi L corresponds to the identity of ΦL\Phi L; the counit εM:ΦΨM→M\varepsilon_M:\Phi\Psi M\to M corresponds to the identity of ΨM\Psi M. In degree zero the counit is evaluation. Derived resolutions supply its meaning on complexes. These are adjunction maps, distinct from an algebra unit or a coalgebra counit.

    The two triangle identities are

    εΦL∘Φ(ηL)=1ΦL,Ψ(εM)∘ηΨM=1ΨM.\varepsilon_{\Phi L}\circ\Phi(\eta_L)=1_{\Phi L}, \qquad \Psi(\varepsilon_M)\circ\eta_{\Psi M}=1_{\Psi M}.

    They express compatibility of the two reconstructions. The functor Φ\Phi is fully faithful precisely when every ηL\eta_L is an equivalence. The functor Ψ\Psi is fully faithful precisely when every εM\varepsilon_M is an equivalence. An equivalence of the two whole categories requires both.

    Already extension of scalars requires the derived tensor. Put R=ℂ[x]R=\mathbb C[x] and K=R/(x)K=R/(x). The free resolution

    [R→xR]⟶K,\bigl[R\xrightarrow{x}R\bigr]\longrightarrow K,

    with the two free terms in degrees −1,0-1,0, gives

    K⊗R𝐋K≃[K→0K]≃K⊕︎K[1].K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}K \simeq\bigl[K\xrightarrow{0}K\bigr] \simeq K\oplus K[1].

    Ordinary tensor retains only the degree-zero copy. The other copy records the relation x=0x=0. This is the simplest instance of the information carried by a bar resolution. Extension and restriction of scalars, with their derived adjunction, are described in the Stacks Project, Example 22.33.6.

    A right dg module PP is K-flat if P⊗BXP\otimes_B X is acyclic whenever the left dg module XX is acyclic. Such a module computes derived tensor on arbitrary coefficients. Dually, a complex JJ is K-injective if its Hom complex from every acyclic complex is acyclic. This condition concerns the whole complex; injectivity of each term alone does not suffice in the unbounded case. See the Stacks Project, §13.31.

    Which representations does the vacuum see?

    Consider H=ℂ[C2]H=\mathbb C[C_2], where C2={1,g}C_2=\{1,g\} and g2=1g^2=1. Maps out of the trivial representation take invariants, the image of the idempotent (1+g)/2(1+g)/2. For the sign representation SS, gg acts by −1-1, so these maps vanish in every derived degree. For S⊗SS\otimes S, gg acts by 11 and the invariants are ℂ\mathbb C. Thus taking vacuum cochains on the two inputs separately can lose a product whose output lies in the vacuum sector.

    There is a corresponding positive statement for a strictly augmented dg bialgebra HH over a characteristic-zero field FF, with an ordinary chain coproduct Δ\Delta. Let TT be a locally nilpotent degree-zero algebra derivation and coalgebra coderivation commuting with the differential, with εT=0\varepsilon T=0. For u∈Fu\in F, use (euT⊗1)Δ(e^{uT}\otimes1)\Delta for the action on M⊗uNM\otimes_u N. Put C(M)=RHomH⁡(F,M)C(M)=\operatorname{RHom}_{H}(F,M), B′=C(F)B'=C(F). Translation on the bar resolution induces a cochain algebra automorphism Θu\Theta_u of B′B'. The translated cup product gives a natural map

    C(M)⊗B′𝐋ΘuC(N)⟶C(M⊗uN).C(M)\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{B'}{}_{\Theta_u}C(N) \longrightarrow C(M\otimes_u N).

    The subscript twists the left B′B'-action on C(N)C(N). Use full products for Hom and algebraic direct sums for the tensor totalizations. The map is an equivalence whenever either module is built from FF by finitely many shifts, cones and retracts. This subcategory, thick⁡(F)\operatorname{thick}(F), is identified by CC with the perfect B′B'-modules. Indeed the bar diagonal gives the map, its unit identities give an equivalence at FF, and exactness propagates it through the finite constructions. If FF is compact as an HH-module, CC also preserves coproducts, extending the conclusion to the subcategory Loc⁡(F)\operatorname{Loc}(F) generated using arbitrary coproducts.

    In the sign example F=ℂF=\mathbb C is compact, and SS lies in the other idempotent summand. The map just displayed on S,SS,S is 0→ℂ0\to\mathbb C. The same failure occurs with nonzero differential and translation. Tensor the group algebra with F[x,y]⊗Λ(e,f)F[x,y]\otimes\Lambda(e,f) on primitive generators, with dx=e, dy=f, Ty=x, Tf=edx=e,\ dy=f,\ Ty=x,\ Tf=e, and all other generator differentials and translations zero. The polynomial and exterior generators have degrees zero and one respectively. The homotopy taking e↦x, f↦ye\mapsto x,\ f\mapsto y as a derivation contracts each positive total polynomial-plus-exterior weight after division by that weight. Hence the augmentation of this extra factor is a quasi-isomorphism. Both signs inflated from the group algebra give the same test at every uu. In the affine problem the regular horizontal top is what permits testing all horizontal highest weights.

    6.2 Affine currents and the algebra acting on their resolution

    Let 𝔤\mathfrak g be a nonzero finite-dimensional simple complex Lie algebra. Choose an invariant form κ\kappa, normalized so that long roots have squared length two, and write

    12tr⁡(ad⁡xad⁡y)=h∨κ(x,y).\tfrac12\operatorname{tr}(\operatorname{ad}x\,\operatorname{ad}y) =h^\vee\kappa(x,y).

    The integer h∨h^\vee is the dual Coxeter number. For a scalar parameter kk, set ℓ=(−k−h∨)κ\ell=(-k-h^\vee)\kappa. The affine mode algebra AℓA_\ell has relations

    [xtr,ytq]=[x,y]tr+q+rδr+q,0ℓ(x,y)1.[xt^r,yt^q]=[x,y]t^{r+q} +r\delta_{r+q,0}\ell(x,y)1.

    The scalar −k−h∨-k-h^\vee is its raw affine level, the coefficient of the central cocycle in this normalization. Write s=−ks=-k for the shifted level, so that the raw scalar level is s−h∨s-h^\vee and B=Y−s(𝔤)B=Y_{-s}(\mathfrak g). The mode algebra here has no degree derivation. Its internal energy grading assigns energy −r-r to xtrxt^r.

    Put

    𝔫=t𝔤[t],𝔩=𝔤[t−1],R=U(𝔤),H=U(𝔩).\mathfrak n=t\mathfrak g[t],\qquad \mathfrak l=\mathfrak g[t^{-1}],\qquad R=U(\mathfrak g),\qquad H=U(\mathfrak l).

    A module is smooth if each vector is annihilated by tN𝔤[t]t^N\mathfrak g[t] for some NN, which may depend on the vector. Consider the induced smooth module

    W=Aℓ⊗U(𝔫)ℂ.W=A_\ell\otimes_{U(\mathfrak n)}\mathbb C.

    The Poincaré–Birkhoff–Witt theorem identifies its underlying vector space with HH. Its energy-zero part is the regular RR-module. This distinguishes WW from the scalar-top vacuum

    V=Aℓ⊗U(𝔤[t])ℂ,V=A_\ell\otimes_{U(\mathfrak g[t])}\mathbb C,

    whose energy-zero part is ℂ\mathbb C.

    The polynomial dg algebra B=Yk(𝔤)B=Y_k(\mathfrak g) has even generators bmab_m^a and odd generators ca,mc_{a,m}, for m≥0m\ge0. Fix a basis tat_a, write [ta,tb]=fabctc[t_a,t_b]=f_{ab}{}^ct_c, and sum repeated Lie-algebra indices. Its relations and differential are

    [bma,bnb]=fabcbm+nc,[bma,cb,n]=−facbcc,m+n,ca,mcb,n=−cb,nca,m,dca,m=12fbca∑r+p=m−1cb,rcc,p,dbma=mkκabcb,m−1+12fabc∑r+p=m−1(cb,rbpc+bpccb,r).\begin{aligned} [b_m^a,b_n^b]&=f_{ab}{}^cb_{m+n}^c,\\ [b_m^a,c_{b,n}]&=-f_{ac}{}^bc_{c,m+n}, &c_{a,m}c_{b,n}&=-c_{b,n}c_{a,m},\\ dc_{a,m}&=\tfrac12f_{bc}{}^a \sum_{r+p=m-1}c_{b,r}c_{c,p},\\ db_m^a&=mk\kappa_{ab}c_{b,m-1} +\tfrac12f_{ab}{}^c \sum_{r+p=m-1}(c_{b,r}b_p^c+b_p^cc_{b,r}). \end{aligned}

    Negative indices contribute nothing. The cohomological degrees of b,cb,c are 0,10,1; their internal weights are m,m+1m,m+1. The differential preserves weight. The odd generators are often called ghosts; here that word means these specified degree-one algebra generators.

    Write BwB_w for the entire weight-ww complex. Then

    B=⨁w≥0Bw,B0=R,I=⨁w>0Bw.B=\bigoplus_{w\ge0}B_w,\qquad B_0=R,\qquad I=\bigoplus_{w>0}B_w.

    There are two useful quotients:

    B→qH→e0R,q(ca,m)=0,q(bma)=tat−m.B\xrightarrow{q}H\xrightarrow{e_0}R,\qquad q(c_{a,m})=0,\quad q(b_m^a)=t_at^{-m}.

    The map e0e_0 kills the strictly negative modes. Thus p=e0qp=e_0q is weight-zero projection and I=ker⁡pI=\ker p. These quotients forget different information. An HH-module inflated along qq has zero ghost action but may have nonzero negative-current action. Inflation from RR kills both.

    The affine Chevalley resolution of WW has

    P−p=Aℓ⊗Λp𝔫.P^{-p}=A_\ell\otimes\Lambda^p\mathfrak n.

    Its differential combines current multiplication with the Lie bracket. For x∈𝔩x\in\mathfrak l, let axa_x be the exterior derivation induced by y↦pr𝔫⁡[x,y]y\mapsto\operatorname{pr}_{\mathfrak n}[x,y]. The generators act on this resolution through

    ρ(bma)=Rtat−m−atat−m,ρ(ca,m)=ιa,m+1,\rho(b_m^a)=R_{t_at^{-m}}-a_{t_at^{-m}}, \qquad \rho(c_{a,m})=\iota_{a,m+1},

    where RxR_x is right multiplication on the affine factor and ιa,m+1\iota_{a,m+1} is contraction with the indicated positive mode. This specified generator action is called the native action. The correction axa_x is essential: its commutator supplies the half-Killing-form shift in ℓ\ell. With the graded opposite composition, these operators give the algebraic derived endomorphism comparison. This construction is developed in A derived endomorphism model for the line algebra, the affine-resolution and generator-lift sections.

    We must specify an additional smooth realization before using ordinary smooth derived Hom. Assume that the operators above are realized by a coherent right-BB object 𝒲\mathcal W in 𝒮ℓ=D(Sm⁡(Aℓ))\mathscr S_\ell=D(\operatorname{Sm}(A_\ell)), with underlying object WW. Assume the prescribed homogeneous endomorphism comparison and the compatible smooth Taylor resolutions

    PN=(Aℓ/Aℓ𝔫N)⊗Λ∙(𝔫/𝔫N),𝔫N=tN𝔤[t],P_N=(A_\ell/A_\ell\mathfrak n_N) \otimes\Lambda^\bullet(\mathfrak n/\mathfrak n_N), \qquad \mathfrak n_N=t^N\mathfrak g[t],

    including their action comparisons on a common sufficiently large cutoff for each finite operator diagram. “Coherent” here includes all the higher compatibility homotopies for the right action. Finally assume the resulting enhanced adjunction

    Φ=𝒲⊗B𝐋−:D(B)⇄𝒮ℓ:Ψ=RHomSm⁡(Aℓ)⁡(𝒲,−).\Phi=\mathcal W\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}-: D(B)\rightleftarrows\mathscr S_\ell: \Psi=\operatorname{RHom}_{\operatorname{Sm}(A_\ell)}(\mathcal W,-).
    (6.1)

    These are the smooth realization hypotheses used below. They identify a particular action and adjunction; they do not assert the desired unit theorem. They also keep smooth derived Hom distinct from derived Hom in all algebraic AℓA_\ell-modules.

    There is a parallel internally graded version. Modules are algebraic direct sums of their energy components, with arbitrary support. Set L⟨r⟩w=Lw−rL\langle r\rangle_w=L_{w-r}. Mapping complexes are formed at a specified homogeneous shift; their outer sum is algebraic. Neither convention introduces an energy completion.

    6.3 Cofree coefficients give the first unit theorem

    The restricted positive-current dual

    C𝔤=⨁E≥0U(𝔫)E∨C_{\mathfrak g}=\bigoplus_{E\ge0}U(\mathfrak n)_E^\vee

    uses the positive current degree deg⁡(xtr)=r\deg(xt^r)=r. Each summand is finite dimensional, and every element of C𝔤C_{\mathfrak g} has finite support in this degree. Put

    (Lxϕ)(u)=ϕ(xu),(Dxϕ)(u)=ϕ(ux).(L_x\phi)(u)=\phi(xu),\qquad (D_x\phi)(u)=\phi(ux).

    Both actions lower the support bound of a functional. For a homogeneous positive-current basis xi=tatrx_i=t_at^r, write ci=ca,r−1c_i=c_{a,r-1}. The complex

    𝒬=C𝔤⊗B,d𝒬(ϕ⊗b)=ϕ⊗db+∑iLxiϕ⊗cib\mathcal Q=C_{\mathfrak g}\otimes B,\qquad d_{\mathcal Q}(\phi\otimes b) =\phi\otimes db+\sum_iL_{x_i}\phi\otimes c_i b
    (6.2)

    has a pointwise finite differential. Its support filtration makes it semifree as a right BB-module: the differential of a new free generator uses generators of smaller support degree.

    The full affine action is restricted coinduction. Using the even HH-action on the underlying graded algebra BB, identify 𝒬\mathcal Q with

    {f∈HomH⁡(Aℓ,B):f|U(𝔫)≥d=0 for some d},(af)(b)=f(ba).\{f\in\operatorname{Hom}_H(A_\ell,B): f|_{U(\mathfrak n)_{\ge d}}=0\text{ for some }d\}, \qquad (af)(b)=f(ba).

    The Poincaré–Birkhoff–Witt decomposition gives the preceding tensor description. The twist in (6.2) makes its differential affine-linear at precisely the level ℓ=(−k−h∨)κ\ell=(-k-h^\vee)\kappa.

    Under the smooth realization hypotheses, 𝒬\mathcal Q is equivalent to the whole coherent right-BB object 𝒲\mathcal W, with its affine action retained. Consequently it computes ΦL\Phi L for every ordinary unbounded LL. This is the cofree-model theorem in The cofree native model and inflated-base unit for every simple Lie algebra. The comparison preserves the specified action on PP.

    If TT is an arbitrary unbounded HH-complex inflated to BB, every ghost acts by zero. Formula (6.2) becomes

    ΦT≃(C𝔤⊗T,1⊗dT).\Phi T\simeq(C_{\mathfrak g}\otimes T,1\otimes d_T).

    Its positive-current action is DD on the first factor. The restricted dual with arbitrary vector-space coefficients is injective in the smooth positive-current category. More is needed for an unbounded TT: split its underlying complex over ℂ\mathbb C into its cohomology and a contractible complex. Tensoring this splitting with C𝔤C_{\mathfrak g} is positive-current-linear. It exhibits the restriction as homotopy equivalent to a product of injectives placed in single degrees, hence as K-injective. At each degree only one of those factors contributes; no completion of C𝔤C_{\mathfrak g} is involved.

    The positive-current invariants are exactly δ1⊗T\delta_1\otimes T, where δ1\delta_1 extracts the scalar coefficient of U(𝔫)U(\mathfrak n). Evaluation on this vector identifies the original signed tensor–Hom unit with the identity of TT.

    Conditional unit theorem for inflated coefficients. For every simple 𝔤\mathfrak g and every k∈ℂk\in\mathbb C, under the smooth realization hypotheses of (6.1), the actual unit

    T→ηTΨΦTT\xrightarrow{\eta_T}\Psi\Phi T

    is an equivalence for every ordinary unbounded HH-complex inflated along qq, and therefore for every inflated RR-complex. This holds with arbitrary algebraic internal support or without an internal grading.

    The theorem includes critical affine level. It also includes raw 𝔰𝔩2\mathfrak{sl}_2 level −3-3. Its proof uses the zero ghost action on these coefficients; the cofree realization formula alone does not establish the unit for a general BB-module.

    6.4 Finite descent from a quotient

    To reach modules with nonzero ghost action, consider first a general split dg algebra extension

    R⟶B→pR,p|R=1,I=ker⁡p.R\longrightarrow B\xrightarrow{p}R,\qquad p|_R=1, \qquad I=\ker p.

    Assume RR is an ordinary algebra, BB is K-flat on both RR-sides, and for a finite integer NN,

    I⊗R𝐋N≃0as a complex of R-bimodules.I^{\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}N}\simeq0 \quad\text{as a complex of \(R\)-bimodules}.
    (6.3)

    The two multiplication actions are part of this assertion; RR need not be central.

    Let F=R⊗B𝐋−F=R\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}-, and let UU be restriction of scalars along pp, also called inflation. A relative bar resolution converts (6.3) into vanishing of the NN-fold derived tensor of II over BB. For every LL, put

    Tj(L)=I⊗B𝐋j⊗B𝐋L,T0(L)=L.T_j(L)=I^{\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}j} \otimes_B^{\mathbf L}L,\qquad T_0(L)=L.

    There is a functorial tower

    0≃TN(L)⟶TN−1(L)⟶⋯⟶T0(L)=L0\simeq T_N(L)\longrightarrow T_{N-1}(L) \longrightarrow\cdots\longrightarrow T_0(L)=L
    (6.4)

    whose triangles are

    Tj+1(L)⟶Tj(L)→uTj(L)UF(Tj(L))⟶Tj+1(L)[1].T_{j+1}(L)\longrightarrow T_j(L) \xrightarrow{u_{T_j(L)}}UF(T_j(L)) \longrightarrow T_{j+1}(L)[1].
    (6.5)

    Here uu is the scalar-extension unit, distinct from η\eta in (6.1). Every cofiber is inflated from an unrestricted RR-complex with its actual outer RR-action.

    The bar argument explains the change of base from RR to BB. Resolve an II-factor by terms

    (I⊗RI⊗Rq⊗RB)[q],q≥0.\bigl(I\otimes_R I^{\otimes_R q}\otimes_R B\bigr)[q], \qquad q\ge0.

    In an NN-fold derived tensor over BB, each resulting bar term contains at least NN copies of II tensored over RR. Such a term is acyclic by (6.3) and the two-sided K-flatness. Finite bar-length filtrations and their exact algebraic union prove the asserted vanishing without a cohomological bound.

    For an exact enhanced adjunction Φ⊣Ψ\Phi\dashv\Psi, the class of objects on which its unit is invertible is closed under finite triangles and retracts. Thus (6.4) proves:

    Finite descent theorem. Under the split-extension, K-flatness and tensor-vanishing hypotheses above, the actual unit is invertible on every L∈D(B)L\in D(B) if it is invertible on every unrestricted inflated RR-complex.

    The proof propagates the same natural transformation through (6.5). It never assumes that Ψ\Psi preserves an infinite coproduct. The construction and its map identifications are given in A finite filtration from derived tensor nilpotence, Theorems A–B.

    Ordinary ideal multiplication cannot replace (6.3). For B=ℂ[ϵ]/(ϵ2)B=\mathbb C[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2), R=ℂR=\mathbb C and I=(ϵ)I=(\epsilon), one has I2=0I^2=0, but

    I⊗ℂN≅ℂ(N≥1).I^{\otimes_{\mathbb C}N}\cong\mathbb C \qquad(N\ge1).

    The multiplication of two ideal elements vanishes; the tensor of those elements remains nonzero.

    There is a second, weaker sufficient criterion. For a dg algebra map B→HB\to H, form its fibre J→B→HJ\to B\to H in the derived category of genuine BB-bimodules. It suffices that one tensor power of the fibre-inclusion map

    μN:J⊗B𝐋N⟶B\mu_N:J^{\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}N}\longrightarrow B
    (6.6)

    be zero as a bimodule morphism, together with invertibility of the unit on all inflated unbounded HH-complexes. The tensor object in (6.6) need not vanish. A fixed bimodule nullhomotopy makes BB a retract of cofib⁡(μN)\operatorname{cofib}(\mu_N); the latter is a finite extension of bimodules whose left action factors through HH. Tensoring this one diagram with LL gives a coefficient-functorial retract and proves the unit theorem. See Finite bimodule descent for the actual adjunction unit, Theorem 1.1.

    6.5 The sharp exponent in every simple affine type

    Let Φ0+\Phi_0^+ be the positive roots of the finite-dimensional simple Lie algebra 𝔤\mathfrak g, with long roots of squared length two. Put D=|Φ0+|D=|\Phi_0^+| and take shifted level s∈ℂ∖ℚs\in\mathbb C\setminus\mathbb Q. Recall R=U(𝔤)R=U(\mathfrak g), B=Y−s(𝔤)B=Y_{-s}(\mathfrak g) and I=⨁m>0BmI=\bigoplus_{m>0}B_m.

    Theorem (sharp tensor exponent). The first vanishing derived tensor power of II over RR is D+1D+1:

    I⊗R𝐋D≄0,I⊗R𝐋(D+1)≃0in D(R⊗Rop).I^{\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}D}\not\simeq0,\qquad I^{\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}(D+1)}\simeq0 \quad\text{in }D(R\otimes R^{\mathrm{op}}).

    This is an assertion about an object with its two multiplication actions. It holds in the algebraic internal grading and after forgetting that grading.

    Why should a root count bound a tensor length? A horizontal Verma module MτM_\tau is the RR-module induced from a highest-weight line for a Borel subalgebra of 𝔤\mathfrak g. For highest-weight calculations the degree derivation is restored by its action −E-E on energy EE. At fixed input energy aa, induce a horizontal module NN to the affine algebra, declaring its positive currents to kill its top. On horizontal category 𝒪\mathcal O, the complex Bm⊗R𝐋NB_m\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}N computes the derived positive-current invariants of this induced module in energy a+ma+m. Here category 𝒪\mathcal O uses finitely generated weight modules with locally finite action of the positive Borel. At each energy the negative-mode and exterior-degree sums are finite. Putting the odd generators first in a Poincaré–Birkhoff–Witt basis identifies them with the cochains on positive modes. The zero modes act on the left both on these cochains and on their coefficients, and act on the right by coefficient multiplication. These are the two actions used in the tensor power.

    Fix an affine highest weight and let μ\mu be its horizontal part shifted by the finite Weyl vector ρ=12∑α>0α\rho=\tfrac12\sum_{\alpha>0}\alpha. A real root α+nδ\alpha+n\delta, where nn is its loop mode, is integral at this weight precisely when

    (μ,α)+ns∈(α,α)2ℤ.(\mu,\alpha)+ns\in\tfrac{(\alpha,\alpha)}2\mathbb Z .

    There is at most one such mode for each α\alpha. More is true. On the rational vector space spanned by 1,s1,s and the finitely many simple-root pairings, choose a rational-linear functional ff with f(1)=0, f(s)=1f(1)=0,\ f(s)=1. Root lengths in the chosen normalization are rational. Thus the mode of every integral root is n=−f((μ,α))n=-f((\mu,\alpha)). All the integral roots lie in the graph of one linear function on their projected root span. Reflection in that graph projects faithfully to reflection in a finite root subsystem. The integral Weyl group W′W' is finite and its longest length is at most DD. This step includes the short roots.

    In a fixed affine block, horizontal linkage classes at their assigned energies are indexed by double cosets WP\W′/WKW_P\backslash W'/W_K. The zero-mode integral roots generate WPW_P, and WKW_K fixes a dominant representative of the affine weight. Each coset has a largest element for the Bruhat order, the order on Weyl elements defined by reduced subwords. The direction of transition can be read from highest-weight modules. A nonzero derived map between standard Verma modules requires downward linkage. This follows by resolving the source with projectives having Verma filtrations and applying the composition-factor criterion to the target. On reflection labels this forces a weak increase in Bruhat order. Taking the largest double-coset representative preserves that order. A surviving BmB_m with m>0m>0 increases the assigned energy, hence changes the coset and strictly increases the length of its largest element. Such a chain has at most DD steps. The finite-block and Verma-embedding theorems used here are given in Fiebig's treatment of affine category 𝒪\mathcal O. Theorems 2.2, 2.3 and 3.10 (arXiv:math/0305378v2).

    To pass from tests on modules to actual bimodules, fix the positive weights m1,…,mjm_1,\ldots,m_j. Each BmiB_{m_i} is bounded, free on either RR-side in each degree, and locally finite for the adjoint action xv−vxxv-vx. The tensor word has finitely generated Harish–Chandra bimodule cohomology, meaning that it retains this local finiteness and both RR-actions. If its highest nonzero cohomology were MM, a nonzero quotient of MM with fixed right central character would survive tensoring with the corresponding dominant horizontal Verma by Bernstein–Gelfand's theorem on Harish–Chandra bimodules. Right exactness in the highest degree detects the original word. Thus vanishing on all these Verma tests implies bimodule vanishing. There are finitely many positive tuples at each total weight, and the algebraic direct sum of the acyclic words is acyclic. This proves the upper bound.

    For sharpness choose the linear function d0d_0 on the root lattice taking value one on each finite simple root. Write d0(α)=(γ,α)d_0(\alpha)=(\gamma,\alpha) and take μ=ρ−sγ\mu=\rho-s\gamma. Every finite root now has its integral lift α+d0(α)δ\alpha+d_0(\alpha)\delta. All positive roots have positive mode, and the weight is regular. Follow a reduced expression for the longest Weyl element from the identity. At the jj-th reflection the positive coroot pairing is an integer qjq_j. Each step gives an actual injection of affine Vermas that sends its horizontal top into the degree-zero cycles of Bqj⊗RMτj−1B_{q_j}\otimes_R M_{\tau_{j-1}}. The composite of the injections remains nonzero. Multiplying the native degree-zero coefficients in the order qD,…,q1q_D,\ldots,q_1 acts on the initial top by this composite. The complex has no negative cochain terms, so its nonzero degree-zero cycle survives in cohomology. This realizes DD positive factors on one choice of top.

    Conditional full-unit theorem. At nonrational shifted level ss, in every finite-dimensional simple complex type, assume the smooth realization (6.1) with its specified right action, common Taylor cutoffs and enhanced homogeneous tensor–Hom comparison. For every ordinary unbounded BB-complex LL the original unit is an equivalence

    ηL:L→∼ΨΦL.\eta_L:L\xrightarrow{\sim}\Psi\Phi L .

    This holds for the ungraded adjunction and for algebraic internal grading with arbitrary support. Algebraically, (6.4) has at most D+1D+1 inflated RR-complex factors. The scalar-extension functor R⊗B𝐋−R\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}- is conservative, since zero base change makes every map Tj+1(L)→Tj(L)T_{j+1}(L)\to T_j(L) an equivalence and TD+1(L)=0T_{D+1}(L)=0. The affine assertion uses the additional fact that (6.1) has its unit invertible on every one of those inflated factors. The naturality squares and the finite triangles propagate precisely that unit to LL.

    Four factors for 𝔰𝔩3\mathfrak{sl}_3

    For the trace form on 𝔰𝔩3\mathfrak{sl}_3 the raw affine level is s−3s-3. The positive roots are α1,α2,α1+α2\alpha_1,\alpha_2,\alpha_1+\alpha_2. The longest Weyl element reverses the three coordinates. Apply its adjacent transpositions 1,2,11,2,1 to ρ=(1,0,−1)\rho=(1,0,-1). The differences in the two entries about to be swapped are 1,2,11,2,1, giving the actual nonzero word B1⊗R𝐋B2⊗R𝐋B1B_1\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}B_2\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}B_1. Thus

    I⊗R𝐋4≃0,I⊗R𝐋3≄0.I^{\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}4}\simeq0,\qquad I^{\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}3}\not\simeq0 .
    (6.7)

    The four-step tower below is this case of (6.4). It also follows from The fourth derived tensor power of the native sl3 positive ideal and The full ordinary native unit for sl3 at nonrational parameter. In type A1A_1 two factors suffice. In A3A_3 a surviving six-factor word has weights 1,2,3,1,2,11,2,3,1,2,1 in tensor order and every seven-factor word vanishes. In B2B_2, G2G_2, F4F_4 and E8E_8 the least vanishing exponents are 5,7,25,1215,7,25,121, respectively.

    6.6 The image and its original counit

    Write Loc⁡(W)\operatorname{Loc}(W) for the smallest full stable subcategory containing WW and closed under arbitrary coproducts and retracts. In the internally graded case use all energy shifts:

    𝒞={Loc𝒮ℓ⁡(W),ungraded,Loc𝒮ℓ⁡{W⟨r⟩:r∈ℤ},graded.\mathscr C= \begin{cases} \operatorname{Loc}_{\mathscr S_\ell}(W),&\text{ungraded},\\ \operatorname{Loc}_{\mathscr S_\ell} \{W\langle r\rangle:r\in\mathbb Z\},&\text{graded}. \end{cases}

    Under the preceding full-unit theorem,

    D(B)≃𝒞.D(B)\simeq\mathscr C.
    (6.8)

    The source is generated by BB, or by all its internal shifts, using semifree resolutions. The left adjoint preserves coproducts and sends these generators to WW and its shifts. Full faithfulness also lifts cones and retracts between image objects. These facts identify the image exactly with 𝒞\mathscr C.

    For every smooth MM, the original counit gives the coreflection into this image,

    ΦΨM→εMM.\Phi\Psi M\xrightarrow{\varepsilon_M}M.

    This means that for every C∈𝒞C\in\mathscr C, it induces an equivalence on derived maps from CC. To prove it, the second triangle identity and the full-unit theorem give

    Ψ(εM)=ηΨM−1.\Psi(\varepsilon_M)=\eta_{\Psi M}^{-1}.

    The cone of εM\varepsilon_M is therefore killed by Ψ\Psi, hence is right-orthogonal to 𝒞\mathscr C. In particular, (6.8) identifies a specified part of the smooth category; it does not assert that every smooth object lies there.

    An object is compact in a category if maps from it commute with arbitrary coproducts. The free module BB is compact in D(B)D(B), so WW is compact inside 𝒞\mathscr C, with all shifts included when graded. Compactness against arbitrary smooth targets would require an additional statement about Ψ\Psi on coproducts in the ambient category.

    6.7 Infinite extensions at other levels

    Finite descent explains why the nonrational theorem reaches unbounded coefficients. Without it, invertibility on every finite stage need not survive an infinite construction.

    At critical raw level −h∨-h^\vee, take B=Y0B=Y_0 and

    E=B⊗R𝐋ℂ,ΦE≃V.E=B\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}\mathbb C,\qquad \Phi E\simeq V.

    Assume the smooth realization and its actual lower-energy unit theorem. Critical vacuum cohomology supplies extension classes

    V⟶V[1]⟨−(n+2)⟩,n≥0,V\longrightarrow V[1]\langle-(n+2)\rangle,\qquad n\ge0,

    whose finite consecutive products are all nonzero. Their construction uses the quadratic central field and its successive derivatives. The level-deformation classes correspond to differentials of independent polynomial coordinates under the Frenkel–Teleman theorem: Self-extensions of Verma modules and differential forms on opers, Theorem 4.4 (arXiv:math/0401428).

    Lift these classes through the unit on the individually lower-weight-bounded objects and form

    L=hocolimr≥0⁡E[r]⟨−r(r+3)2⟩.L=\operatorname*{hocolim}_{r\ge0} E[r]\left\langle-\frac{r(r+3)}2\right\rangle.
    (6.9)

    A sequential homotopy colimit is the cone of 1−shift1-\mathrm{shift} on the direct sum of its terms. Compactness of EE detects a nonzero map E→LE\to L: its successive representatives are precisely the nonzero extension products. Thus L≠0L\ne0.

    After realization, the terms are shifted copies of the module VV, concentrated in different cohomological degrees. Every transition induces zero on cohomology, so 1−shift1-\mathrm{shift} induces the identity on the cohomology of the direct sum. Its cone is zero. Consequently

    L≠0,ΦL=0,ηL:L⟶0.L\ne0,\qquad \Phi L=0,\qquad \eta_L:L\longrightarrow0.

    The lower weight bounds in (6.9) tend to minus infinity. Each finite stage keeps its valid unit. This is the theorem of A critical-level kernel of the ordinary first-kind realization, §§1–4, conditional on its specified smooth realization and lower-energy comparison.

    Related extension telescopes give kernels at raw 𝔰𝔩2\mathfrak{sl}_2 levels −4,−5,…-4,-5,\ldots, and at raw level −2h∨-2h^\vee for every simple type, under the corresponding realization and lower-energy hypotheses. They also show that WW can fail to be compact even in its own generated category. The precise sources are Actual-unit kernels at negative integral shifted sl2 levels and A noncritical ordinary-unit kernel for every simple Lie algebra.

    These ordinary-derived statements coexist with an all-type, all-level induction equivalence using different weak equivalences. For dg YkY_k-modules that are termwise algebraically smooth for the even modes, twisted induction at raw level k−h∨k-h^\vee has an explicit restricted twisted-coinduction inverse after inverting exactly the maps that induction sends to affine quasi-isomorphisms. That class is a proper subclass of the ordinary quasi-isomorphisms. This source localization therefore retains information that localization at all ordinary quasi-isomorphisms discards. This is the equivalence in Corrected induction: the inverse, the adjunction and the equivalence, Theorem 8.1. Its functor, level convention and source localization are part of the statement.

    There is also a polarized duality for the universal mode algebra. Its input is a Tate Lie algebra with continuous bracket, an open linearly compact positive subalgebra with a countable basis of finite-codimensional ideals, countable-dimensional quotient, and a continuous central cocycle η\eta vanishing on two positive inputs. Its smooth complexes at central generator one are taken modulo those coacyclic after restriction to the positive subalgebra. Here coacyclic means generated from totalizations of short exact sequences by triangles, coproducts and retracts. The dual consists of curved contramodules, with projective underlying graded contramodule and the corresponding Becker-coacyclic positive reductions killed. The curved differential on the cochain algebra has curvature +η+\eta, and a free contramodule uses an inverse limit of direct sums in each total degree. Over ℂ\mathbb C, the complementary category in the semi-infinite pairing is at affine scalar level −ℓ0−2h∨-\ell_0-2h^\vee for original scalar level ℓ0\ell_0, or at Virasoro charge 26−c26-c. For instance ℓ0=−h∨\ell_0=-h^\vee is a fixed point of the affine involution, while the cocycle mℓ0κ(x,y)δm+n,0m\ell_0\kappa(x,y)\delta_{m+n,0} still acts on opposite modes. The ordinary unit (6.1), these polarized quotients and the passage from universal modes to simple vertex-algebra quotients each require their specified functors.

    At rational shift the zero-weight test has no finite exponent

    For any rational shifted level s=a/bs=a/b, with integers a,ba,b, b>0b>0, choose a long root α\alpha. Both α+bδ\alpha+b\delta and −α+bδ-\alpha+b\delta are positive affine roots. Choose an integral initial pairing u=(μ,α)u=(\mu,\alpha), and reflect in these roots alternately. In the first step the shifted coroot pairing is u+au+a and the new horizontal pairing is −u−2a-u-2a. The next coroot pairing is u+3au+3a. In general the jj-th pairing and its energy increase are

    qj=u+(2j−1)a,mj=bqj.q_j=u+(2j-1)a,\qquad m_j=bq_j .

    For any prescribed finite length NN one can take uu large enough that all qj>0q_j>0 for 1≤j≤N1\le j\le N. The required step is an injection M(ξ−qβ)↪M(ξ)M(\xi-q\beta)\hookrightarrow M(\xi) when a positive real root β\beta has ⟨ξ+ρˆ,β∨⟩=q∈ℤ>0\langle\xi+\widehat\rho,\beta^\vee\rangle=q\in\mathbb Z_{>0}. Here ρˆ\widehat\rho pairs to one with the affine simple coroots. Kübel's Theorem 4.1 gives the ordinary Verma composition-factor criterion. For the single-root injection one can argue directly, including at a critical or singular intersection. On the whole coroot hyperplane take the fixed finite PBW space of negative words of weight −qβ-q\beta. The matrix of the simple raising operators on that space has polynomial entries in the highest weight. Existence of a nonzero singular vector is closed, by its maximal minors. Away from the critical hyperplane and the countably many other real-root hyperplanes, the ordinary noncritical block has just the two labels ξ,ξ−qβ\xi,\xi-q\beta. Fiebig's Verma-embedding theorem there gives a nonzero kernel on a dense subset of the coroot hyperplane, so it persists everywhere on it. Central level varies in this density argument. On specializing to the desired level, multiplication by any surviving singular vector injects the Verma, since the enveloping algebra of the negative part has a polynomial associated graded and hence no zero divisors. Only existence of a singular vector passes to this specialization.

    These injections give a positive-weight word with nonzero composite on a horizontal highest-weight vector. This includes a=0, b=1a=0,\ b=1. Hence at every rational shift and in every simple type I⊗R𝐋N≠0I^{\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}N}\ne0 for all NN. In fact the genuine BB-bimodule map I⊗B𝐋N→BI^{\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}N}\to B is nonzero. Its restriction receives the RR-tensor word by inserting zero-length terms at the intermediate relative bar resolutions, and the composite is exactly the tested multiplication. These finite nonvanishings exclude the descent proof through B→RB\to R. The ghost quotient has a different fibre, and neither finite test alone decides the unit at a rational level.

    6.8 Raw level minus three distinguishes the two quotients

    For 𝔰𝔩2\mathfrak{sl}_2 at raw level −3-3, the line algebra is B=Y1B=Y_1. Let

    Vj=V(−2j−1),Fj=(B⊗RVj)⟨−j2⟩,V_j=V(-2j-1),\qquad F_j=(B\otimes_RV_j)\langle-j^2\rangle,

    where V(λ)V(\lambda) is the horizontal Verma module of highest weight λ\lambda. There are actual degree-zero maps βj:Fj−1→Fj\beta_j:F_{j-1}\to F_j represented by positive-weight cycles. Their affine realizations send highest vectors to

    vj−1⟼f02j−2e−12j−1vj.v_{j-1}\longmapsto f_0^{\,2j-2}e_{-1}^{\,2j-1}v_j.
    (6.10)

    Here f0f_0 is the horizontal lowering current and e−1e_{-1} the mode-−1-1 raising current. These are injective maps of affine Verma modules.

    For L=hocolimj⁡(Fj,βj)L=\operatorname{hocolim}_j(F_j,\beta_j), the two quotients have different effects:

    R⊗B𝐋L=0,H⊗B𝐋L≠0,ΦL≠0.R\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}L=0,\qquad H\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}L\ne0,\qquad \Phi L\ne0.
