    18.1 The physical adjunction and its full domain

    Problem 18.1. Compare the functor defined by the prescribed physical boundary or interface with the tensor–Hom realization of the line algebra, including its right adjoint, unit and counit on the original complexes. Determine its essential image and its compatibility with the position-dependent product of line operators.

    The algebraic unit is known for every simple complex Lie algebra 𝔤\mathfrak g at nonrational shifted level under the native smooth, right-action and tensor–Hom realization hypotheses of Chapter 6. With R=U(𝔤)R=U(\mathfrak g), positive-weight ideal II and D=|Φ+(𝔤)|D=|\Phi^+(\mathfrak g)|, the first vanishing derived tensor power of II over RR is precisely D+1D+1. This proves the unit on each ordinary unbounded source and identifies the image as the localizing category of the regular-top module, including internal shifts in the graded convention. At raw 𝔰𝔩2\mathfrak{sl}_2 level −3-3, the weight-zero quotient kills a particular nonzero telescope on which the original unit is an equivalence. A classification of all sources there is open. At several other rational levels nonzero sources genuinely have zero affine realization. Ordinary induction and its boundary

    The physical interface has a stronger test already through ℏ3=0\hbar^3=0. Use the four current colours of 𝔤𝔩2\mathfrak{gl}_2, including the trace and its exterior ghost modes. At fixed K≠−2K\ne-2, the normalized discrepancy between the two retained kernels is a coboundary in every rooted degree. Its extension to marked Laurent coefficients uses one lower bound, one ghost cutoff and finite right support for the whole series on each input and quotient. On the positive traceless inserted summand the state and Casimir operations are prescribed as part of the comparison. An independent field theory would have to produce them. At K=−2K=-2 there is a translation-compatible linear identification of the critical state complex, with additional critical states that do not occur in the noncritical small complex. It does not identify their marked field operations. The full marked comparison

    One route starts with the physical cut defining the two boundary conditions. Construct its functors, take the two ordered products of independently prepared inputs, and compare their transport with the algebraic unit, counit and tensorator. Another starts from a system of coefficient maps with its collision attachments, constructs the induced interface, and compares it with that same cut. The second route only has physical content if the cut remains independently specified. For a first decisive measurement, retain a positive traceless insertion, a trace creator and a first normal derivative at a collision of slots one and three with slot two kept as spectator. Test both spatial orders, the two occupied vacua and the outgoing vacuum. A covariant lift of the old quotient-inflated module already fails on the trace creator. In the retained coefficient pairing that same creator acts by contraction. Those two operations live on different sides of the pairing. The specified endpoint obstruction

    The unbounded essential-image problem is equally precise. The cellular category, the full subcategory with torsion cohomology, and the derived category of the torsion abelian category are three different constructions. A proposed identification must survive the product-modulo-sum class of Chapter 6. Termwise torsion and bounded-below torsion cohomology already give positive cellularity theorems; those results do not remove the unbounded comparison.

    For algebraically energy-graded positive-current 𝔰𝔩2\mathfrak{sl}_2, a common annihilating tail on all sufficiently low cohomology now makes the actual smooth-vector completion unit invertible. This does not prove generation by the shifted trivial modules: a nonzero torsion-null object could still be complete. The common-tail theorem and its generation boundary.

    18.2 General chiral quantum groups and completed curved duality

    Problem 18.2. For the independently defined chiral field and mode constructions, construct a compatible associative product, same-position tensor, coproduct and exchange on the required category of representations. Identify the relevant curved dual category and the exact localization in which its comparison functors are inverse.

    The spectral class already has explicit fields, a cross-contracted tensor product, level-indexed coproducts, their coassociativity and counit identities, and a field hexagon. The rational determinant-one matrix comparison holds in every rank N≥2N\ge2 and at every numerical level, with divided integral relations and ℏ\hbar-adic fields. Nonlinear quadratic–linear–scalar algebras have derivative-corrected curved transposes. The regular universal W3W_3 mode algebra has actual curved bar adjoints at every finite charge. Chapter 12

    The difference between a field representation and its full mode algebra is already visible at rank two. Start with the determinant-one relations for creation and annihilation matrices and take their prescribed Cauchy modes in the intrinsic algebra of all finite configurations, with the local vacuum normalized. Divide the mixed relation by ℏ2\hbar^2 and the determinant defect by ℏ\hbar before reducing modulo ℏ2\hbar^2. At this precision and every numerical level, the resulting algebra map is injective and has proper image. A two-point diagonal-pole mode survives in the target beyond the Cauchy subalgebra. To reach the next coefficient one can compute the undivided order-four mixed defect directly with all residue relations. Alternatively one can seek a separating family of smooth representations for the Cauchy subalgebra. Applying that strategy to the entire intrinsic algebra would already miss a surviving mode invisible on the indicated states. Intrinsic modes

    The remaining module comparison must preserve the full mixed curvature, rather than only the regular half-ghost quotient. It must specify the summation monad, completed tensors and weak equivalences. A contramodule need not come with an underlying topology, and an ordinary state-field theorem does not decide those choices. For W3W_3, the known smooth objects and iterated-continuous derived Hom provide concrete tests for the proposed localization.

    At the four exceptional shifted levels τ=±3/2,±2/3\tau=\pm3/2,\pm2/3, the universal W4W_4 vacuum gives a finite test of what a derived dual retains. The two torsion summands in local-family cohomological degrees nine and twelve are each killed by one power of the local parameter. Indeed the first derivative of the native vacuum differential has a nonzero pairing between the right and left null spaces in outgoing degrees eight and eleven. Each detecting differential has just one nonunit elementary divisor, so that divisor has order one. The reciprocal local-family map transfers the calculation to the reciprocal levels. The coupled vertex operation gives the graded-commutative Yoneda product, including the degree-three strings on either side and η5η7=0\eta_5\eta_7=0. At the positive exceptional fibre the product of the degree-seven primitive with the additional degree-eight class reduces to one remaining possible scalar in top degree. Its value and the higher operations that would decide associative formality are distinct questions. The exceptional vacuum

    18.3 Universal actions and higher residue compatibility

    Problem 18.3. Decide whether multiplication and vacuum evaluation identify the full character and action spaces for every admitted pointed factorizing actor, and construct a comparison with the ordinary vertex-algebra mapping spaces wherever the two descriptions are claimed to agree.

    For the geometric spaces of Chapter 7, the maps are

    Θ(g)=m(g⊗!1),Ψ(α)=α(1⊗!uB).\Theta(g)=m(g\otimes^!1), \qquad \Psi(\alpha)=\alpha(1\otimes^!u_B).

    Their types, pointings and homotopy fibres are fixed. Recognition is established on the stated unital, module-extension and nonunital families. The original pointed three-block boundary is filled for arbitrary unbounded coassociative actors without a cocommutativity hypothesis. A different separated-base primitive comparison uses coherent cocommutativity of the underlying actor. The general question still requires all root changes, collision restrictions and arbitrarily long refinements.

    For any finite number of degree-one exterior generators, with differential and translation zero on the source, one can calculate its ordinary algebraic mapping space into arbitrary ordinary algebraic targets. On the scalar target, with rr generators, its components are parametrized by ℂr+(r2)\mathbb C^{r+\binom r2}, and each has the homotopy type K(ℂr,1)K(\mathbb C^r,1). The additional (r2)\binom r2 coordinates record pairs of distinct colours. This calculation uses actual factorizations of locality transitions and an ordinary resolution with higher subset generators. To compare it with the geometric problem one must transport both legs of a roof, its vacuum path, and all boundary refinements through changes of root. Pointed actions

    The residue complexes supply a concrete higher-dimensional problem. For Dr,q(b,N;μ)D_{r,q}(b,N;\mu), the strict statement is

    Hn(Dr,q)=0(q≥2, n<q),H^n(D_{r,q})=0\qquad(q\ge2,\ n<q),
    (18.1)

    with positive odd μ\mu and the specified pole bounds. It holds for three spectators with arbitrary nonnegative bounds, for two spectators, and for arbitrary spectator count when the marked–spectator bounds vanish; further fixed positive-bound cases are known. The uniform first compatibility ideal is also computed. The second and later compatibility defects at arbitrary spectator count remain distinct questions. A fixed-bound class Φ\Phi for two spectators at charge four and n=qn=q prevents replacing the strict inequality by n≤qn\le q. Under the transitions that enlarge its pole bound, t[Φ]≠0t[\Phi]\ne0 but t2[Φ]=0t^2[\Phi]=0. This particular obstruction disappears after two transitions. Chapter 7

    There is a sharper result when all four spectator pole bounds are one and μ=1\mu=1. At unshifted lattice N=0N=0, let GmG_m be the kernel of the map from the four triple collision images to the final image, modulo the image of the six pair collisions, with mm marks. Then Gm=0G_m=0 for every mm over the original polynomial base. For a quadratic marked polynomial, explicit resolutions bound the projective dimensions of the pair and triple images tightly enough to exclude the only possible support of a defect. With more marks a surviving associated prime would have to give a double contact. On an étale chart the other roots are disjoint there, so the calculation reduces to the quadratic case. This proves compatibility of these actual images. For general spectator ranks or larger positive pole orders the same vanishing still needs a proof. Even at four simple bounds the two-selected column on five marks gives a separate charge-seven question under the original amplitude hypotheses. Higher residues and their supports

    The genuine Heisenberg actor comparison has a more concrete remaining test. Let F0F^0 be the whole zero sector of its charge and constant detector, and let UU be the genuine pointed automorphism space of H⊕︎ϵHH\oplus\epsilon H acting trivially on state cohomology. The original qBq_B is an equivalence exactly when F0F^0 is connected and UU is contractible. Neither condition is settled; based loop calculations alone cannot see an additional zero-sector component. Genuine fibre reduction.

    18.4 Integral collisions and independently completed intermediate objects

    A triple point can already distinguish a split irregular connection from a nonsplit one with the same ordinary monodromy. The next comparison must retain the directed maps from the collision branches, with their sector frames and the radial class. These determine what can enter the two ordered cuts. The triple-point calculation

    Problem 18.4. Construct the comparison between the integral collision objects, the common radial current construction and independently defined nested tensor products, preserving the original rational evaluations and all incoming and outgoing actions.

    Under the coherent realization, full-unit, bounded-below cellularity and two-term inflated-descent hypotheses stated in Chapter 8, its theorem covers every finite number of radial inputs on the declared F((q))F((q)) domain and original jointly nilpotent smooth tests. The complete incoming bar has its own perturbative contraction; the outgoing realization uses a separate algebraic bar. Finite integral heads have actual derived base-change and collision maps. These are different pieces of the comparison, not absent operations waiting to be defined from scratch.

    The obstruction is equally explicit: the radial field admits coefficient sequences for which substitution into a nested separation has no lower Laurent bound. A valid extension must prove a uniform support condition on its own space, or construct a different map that retains the same evaluations. Collision specialization must be performed before inverting the discriminant. An argument that substitutes a collision into the separated Laurent field has not reached the integral question.

    The full three-pole rational tensorator and native joint comparison hold for arbitrary constant ordinary inputs under the retained realization hypotheses. The independent and joint middle objects are equivalent when the spectator has finite total cohomology. For arbitrary constant T=T12⊗M3T=T_{12}\otimes M_3, there is nevertheless an actual common domain LDfac=LD∩N1L_D^{\mathrm{fac}}=L_D\cap N_1: at each outer Laurent coefficient the spectator has finite algebraic support across the inner series. It maps to the radial object and the independently completed pair-first object. Finite total cohomology of M3M_3 makes its inclusion into LDL_D a quasi-isomorphism; the raw comparison cones remain, and the inflated regular UU-module still gives a nonzero joint/factorized defect. The defined carriers and common-domain theorem.

    Two independently completed pairs also have an algebraic comparison, with separate factorized, symmetric and ordered carriers. Finite total cohomology of both pairs gives equivalences after the specified extensions to either ordered field. The factorized conic intersection uses the smaller ring D∗=Dcon∩Λfac((q))D_*=D_{\mathrm{con}}\cap\Lambda_{\mathrm{fac}}((q)), defined by the conic and separated-cluster support conditions; it is generally not a module over all of DconD_{\mathrm{con}}. The full four-pole rational tensorator has its algebraic bar identities. A native full-bar interchange, its compatibility with associativity in larger trees and its original topology remain further constructions. Two independently completed clusters.

    The factorwise free-bar resolution now evaluates the full three-pole rational current on the algebraic pair-first intersection. A product of the two bar resolutions does the same for two independently completed pairs at four poles. These constructions include a regular input and keep the endpoint actions. Their common graph-domain maps do not establish continuity of unrestricted independent iterates on the original outer topology. On an integral normal coordinate tt, the occupied vacuum projection can retain a first derivative even though, before projection, a regular middle current has a surviving pole −t−1H0-t^{-1}H_0, with H0H_0 its zero mode. One approach is to construct a common continuous recipient for the independent outputs. Another compares the two unprojected ternary maps at each finite integral jet, including the transitions as the cutoff grows, and then controls their inverse limit. Reproducing the occupied derivative without the middle pole would test only the projected diagram. The common domain and the four-point intersection

    For ordinary flat states over a characteristic-zero coefficient algebra with a free vacuum summand and exact finite-state rational exchange, the finite configuration problem has its own complete answer. The word and Spencer complexes have the maps of every surjection, including 13|213\mid2. The direct-sum shuffle integral has a unital associative product and its degree-zero cohomology is the intrinsic mode quotient over the original base. A properly supported integral or a de Rham pushforward from a separately defined Ran space of finite subsets would have to be compared with this object. A successful global construction must recover the finite support counit on the nonconsecutive collision and the spectator derivative before passing to coinvariants. The finite original-base integral

    Normalized-vacuum deletion is available in all three slots on full ambient field tests and constant ground-field tests for DD. For the third slot, translating the coordinate at infinity gives a strict comparison with the anchored two-survivor operation on the transported smooth test. Constant spectral inputs at any finite number of points have a flat chain connection, with outgoing horizontality up to specified homotopies. For the anchored inner complex EE over FF and outer parameter ss, scalar extension F((s))⊗FE→E((s))F((s))\otimes_F E\to E((s)) misses the series whose cohomology coefficients have infinite FF-span. It is a quasi-isomorphism exactly when each individual Hi(E)H^i(E) is finite-dimensional. Integral deletion before projection, the full regular ternary iterates and their coherent action on all trees require further maps. Deletion and the spectral connection.

    For mixed boundary currents, the required domain also includes real height gates and distributional contacts. The finite marked Ward calculus, radial circuit transport and normalized endpoint refinements are established with their stated support and regularity. A general C2C^2 height trace without a retained real normal fails; stronger spectator hypotheses give positive trace results. The next comparison must retain these different domains rather than erase them by calling every operation a distribution. Chapter 8 and Chapter 9

    There is an endpoint version even for the nonzero-level Heisenberg current. Allow a line charge to be a finite-dimensional endomorphism QQ, so that two endpoints can carry cancelling Jordan charges. On the regular energy completion a nonzero off-diagonal entry of the differential at the first pole can vanish in every finite Taylor quotient. Conversely a binary homotopy that cancels a ghost term on a separated Laurent stage need not be continuous on that completion. One route constructs the endpoint category directly with its two occupied vacua and compares it with the polynomial line action. Another builds the varying-vacuum bar and proves its normalized cells agree with the geometric cuts on their common domain. Both must recover the Jordan entry on the overlap before reducing to finite jets. Endpoints and mixed boundaries

    Problem 18.5. Extend analytic conformal-block composition to the required unsmoothed source and target spaces, with both descent conditions and all composition maps retained.

    Consider real central charge c>1c>1 and positive principal labels. Assume the normalized algebraic four-point channel sewings, their canonical spectral L2L^2 vectors, the real unitary channel transform and the positive-label pentagon of Chapter 10. There are receiving graph domains on which two independently formed composites sew, including a balanced diagonal vacuum coefficient. Three positive composites can also be rotated in their common radial overlap. With four original positive inputs at 0,t,y,10,t,y,1, 0<t<y<1/20<t<y<1/2, the independent root charts compare the 14|2314\mid23 and 34|1234\mid12 vacuum channels on a common Hilbert–Schmidt stage, including a weight-two vacuum descendant. A proof on general composite inputs must transport the vacuum and meromorphic components that their positive projections can forget. A route via completion would have to control those components on the receiving topology. A route via independent rooted sewings would have to show that their limits agree on that same topology. Sewing and its domains

    18.5 The compact elliptic attachment

    Problem 18.6. Identify the original compact output with the independently specified elliptic evaluation on the full supported contact image, preserving the cylinder comparison and all prescribed lower homotopies.

    The reduction in Chapter 9 isolates the actual remaining map:

    Aϵδu−Eϵδc=∂ℒϵ+γϵgrδc,γϵ=Aϵjqjr−Eϵjr.A_\epsilon\delta_u-E_\epsilon\delta_c =\partial\mathcal L_\epsilon +\gamma_\epsilon g_r\delta_c, \qquad \gamma_\epsilon=A_\epsilon j_qj_r-E_\epsilon j_r.
    (18.2)

    All terms have the original coefficient and support domains described there. Thus the task is to control γϵ\gamma_\epsilon on that image and to provide the cylinder map on the homotopy outputs where it is needed. A coordinate identification of finite normal spaces is not that cylinder map.

    The full Hom differential retains the antiholomorphic descendants of scalar rows. At cubic order the formal convolution is

    Ω0P3+Ω1P2+Ω2P1+Ω3P0\Omega_0P_3+\Omega_1P_2+\Omega_2P_1+\Omega_3P_0

    in which the supplied presentation gives Ω3=0\Omega_3=0. The first three terms remain to be evaluated on the indicated inputs. Adjusting lower homotopies contributes −∂1S2−∂2S1−∂3S0-\partial_1S_2-\partial_2S_1-\partial_3S_0. The finite polynomial boundary limits, supported compositions and vanishing scalar comparison values remain useful theorems. They do not determine these remaining maps after a scalar trace has discarded their outputs.

    A small test already separates a scalar calculation from the compact attachment. On the zero incoming-jet row with an old pair, a selected new pair and an unselected spectator pair, the three prescribed scalar summands vanish after the stated projection. Applying the source differential to a section before projection leaves an additional protected contact in one rooted order. An independent compact marking must therefore be evaluated on the entire signed sum of its eight ordered anchors, retaining the differential and the old cylinder wherever that cylinder acts. An alternative constructs the full comparison of the two orders directly on a differential-stable space of contact forms. Agreement on the projected scalar alone is consistent with different answers on the distinguished contact.

    18.6 The gravitational state, line and cap

    Problem 18.7. Compare the numerical bulk state, the original based vacuum line and the state prepared by the prescribed geometric filling, on a common field and source domain and with cutting and gluing preserved.

    The normalized numerical Gaussian and its full graded Wick moments are constructed on the original continued cycles. The coefficient heat has a finite part and a based local line section, with the correct covariant source counterterm. The ordinary zero-height finite-stage Ward identity and first quantum heat cells retain the complete first transport term. None of these results needs to be replaced by a formal covariance chosen after the integral. Chapter 11

    On the square-zero reflected Ward family, a common gapped positive-level interval and the fixed-scale uniform inserted heat expansion give the relative formula Wfp(x1)−Wfp(x0)=∫x0x1cF(x)dx/xW_{\mathrm{fp}}(x_1)-W_{\mathrm{fp}}(x_0)=\int_{x_0}^{x_1}c_F(x)\,dx/x. The absolute Mellin comparison retains γEC\gamma_E C. This positive-interval theorem supplies neither a zero-level endpoint estimate nor an independent geometric cap. On a sufficiently small common based family the local line and normalized numerical state do form a continuous line-valued functional; identifying it with the cap remains the stated problem. Positive-level variation and its endpoint.

    The missing cap comparison must supply the map from uncut coefficient fields to the fields on the geometric cut, identify the amplitude lines and transport the normalized observable functionals together with the base amplitude. A global line statement must determine holonomy and anomaly data beyond one local source neighbourhood. An interacting boundary theorem must extend the insertion identities to its actual normal derivatives, positive-height roots, singular higher collisions and quantum orders. The existing ordinary unary result does not assert those extensions.

    An independent cap predicts more than a determinant. A multiplier in an amplitude line cancels from every normalized covariance. Two normalized functionals can agree on all closed linear probes while differing on a fixed off-shell quadratic insertion. Conversely, two centered continuous Gaussian functionals with matching covariance and the same graded Wick recursion agree on every polynomial, and then on their common completion. A direct cut construction can therefore test a complete polarized quartet and a stress pair before passing to all modes, while a characterization by Ward identities must prove that the independently prepared cap satisfies the recursion and the same sewing law. A free disk, whose action and normalization are specified separately from its incoming rays, illustrates both sides of this comparison. Independent preparations

    One precise issue is the relation between formal perturbation and the numerical cycle limit. At a finite spectral window, the covariance correction and determinant-line ratio give an actual formal comparison. An infinite-dimensional conclusion needs convergence of the original series in the same topology and identification of its sum with the numerical state. Equality of finite formal coefficients alone does not establish that analytic statement.

    18.7 Brane junctions and geometric state operations

    Problem 18.8. Construct the open–closed map from the independently specified bulk fields to the derived operations on branes and interfaces, preserving both outer actions, junction composition and the flux class.

    For the M2 particle junction, the degree-two cap onto ANA_N is a split bimodule surjection at every positive rank and nonzero numerical ℏ\hbar. Its kernel multiplicities for N≥2N\ge2 and the higher algebra structure on the full derived tensor product remain unknown. The cap does not make the derived multiplication an equivalence. The integral curved matrix comparison and polynomial Hamiltonian transport supply different positive constructions on their declared rank and degree ranges. The physical comparison must carry the actual fields into these objects. Chapter 14

    The fixed nonzero M2 flux class has square zero as an algebraic Yoneda operation on the full polynomial jet algebra. Its Chevalley cochain primitive can be constructed with an algebraic linear splitting. A primitive for the prescribed representative cannot have uniformly bounded spatial jet order. A pair of actual flux insertions on a five-dimensional interval would thus decide a separate question. One may try to realize the algebraic nullhomotopy with the physical regularity and supports, or exhibit a contact term at a retained spatial jet which obstructs it. Neither the vanishing square nor the split degree-two cap determines the higher interval algebra.

    For the D3 sector, the exact chiral image and simplicity are known, together with specific higher torsion and nonseparated phenomena. A comparison to an independently defined Kodaira–Spencer bulk must preserve that derived information. For surface fusion, the rank-addition Miura map is algebraically coassociative, but its identification with the five-dimensional fusion operation needs the quantized defect, Ward identities and normalization. Higher-current and celestial constructions likewise have explicit finite or special nonabelian scopes; their extension must retain the central and anomaly terms present there.

    Problem 18.9. Compare the critical Hall coefficient theory with the full compact state theory before taking traces, preserving orientation roots, relative moment values, the ordinary unit, pairing and reduced three-boundary operation.

    The ordinary K3 composition Hall comparison is faithful, strong orientation exists on the stated two-charge component group, and the spherical reduced coefficient maps are constructed in every positive length. Relative Donaldson–Thomas operators, untraced multiple covers and the primitive inverse-Igusa trace are also established. The global flag comparison must still retain its common lifting gerbes and relative moment parameters; imposing separate zero moments on every intermediate object would change it.

    One seemingly nearer obstacle admits an exact solution on its own coefficient ring. For the one-loop polynomial Hall algebra the map from the cobar of the finite-root-jet coefficient coalgebra to the divided-factorial shuffle quotient is a quasi-isomorphism in every charge over the polynomial parameter. The source is a direct sum of finite root jets. Passing to infinite support changes it. An oriented critical Hall operator still needs its arrow on the supported flag correspondence before proper direct image. In the two-charge local chart the two nodal branches and both odd normal directions give a concrete comparison with the binary input before projection. A second route would construct the independently defined boundary fields on the same chart and compare their normal operation with that supported arrow. The one-loop map

    The state-map target is H∗(S[d])H^*(S^{[d]}) with its actual pairing and products. At d=1d=1, the trace-invisible cyclic deformation of Chapter 15 changes a nonzero three-state coefficient while keeping the stated trace data. A realization must distinguish those products and preserve the geometric one. Equivariant orientation descent and comparison with independently chosen compact orientations are further specified arrows, not consequences of an orientation sign on numerical charges. Chapter 15

    18.8 Arithmetic positivity and local operations

    Problem 18.10. Establish

    W(g∗g∗)≥0for every g∈Cc∞(ℝ;ℂ),W(g*g^*)\ge0\qquad\text{for every }g\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R;\mathbb C),

    or construct an independently defined ordinary positive representation whose trace is the complete Weil functional on its stated test algebra.

    The exact missing contribution in the existing positive representation is

    W(f)−Tr⁡πcrit(f)=∑wρ∉ℝmρfˆ(wρ).W(f)-\operatorname{Tr}\pi_{\mathrm{crit}}(f) =\sum_{w_\rho\notin\mathbb R}m_\rho\widehat f(w_\rho).
    (18.3)

    Its vanishing on all tests has Riemann-hypothesis strength. The fixed whole-window theorem already proves positivity for every complex L2L^2 test supported in an interval of width at most 31/1031/10, with both parity certificates and full coupling bounds. A theorem on larger cofinal windows must retain the prime-power, polar, real-place and off-block terms. For a block decomposition, the relevant form is the Schur complement A−K∗D−1KA-K^*D^{-1}K; positivity of AA alone is not its required lower bound. Chapter 16

    There is also one fixed compactly supported smooth function ϕ\phi, chosen without using any zeta zero, for which the family gn=ϕ+ϕ(⋅−log⁡n)g_n=\phi+\phi(\,\cdot-\log n) suffices. Eventual nonnegativity of W(gn∗gn∗)W(g_n*g_n^*) is equivalent to the Riemann hypothesis. The Fourier–Laplace transform of the chosen bump is nonvanishing throughout the critical strip, so no zero can disappear from the test by a fortuitous zero of its weight. The two translates have an off-diagonal pairing containing the prime-power terms. Bounding that pairing for all sufficiently large integers remains the arithmetic question. A finite interval of positive values and positivity of each bump separately leave it undecided.

    Problem 18.11. Compare the independently defined arithmetic coefficient complexes with a local field theory and a common integrable trace domain, preserving multiplicity jets, normal operations, Frobenius variance, collisions and the vacuum.

    Continuous integer-summation duality, the full theta trace, actual completed bar homotopies and injective integral normal comparisons are available. The linking construction gives a cyclic vector and nonlocal creation fields; it does not give locality. At an arithmetic point, the relation h0h_0 vanishes on scalar evaluation but its first normal derivative is −p-p, nonzero modulo p2p^2. A local comparison factoring only through scalar points would destroy that operation. A full cyclic trace on the position–normal algebra is also constrained by [D0,Mx0]=pI[D_0,M_{x_0}]=pI, whereas proper trace ideals and specified finite residue functionals remain valid.

    A useful order for these comparisons follows from what they would enable. An independently defined interface giving the two native products would supply the missing physical arrow in the marked example. A fusion that can receive its own products on their original domains would let that arrow be composed through a tree of collisions. A proof identifying the full smooth image would then say which boundary systems this construction can recover. The gravitational filling has another independent demand, a spatial cut that identifies both the phase and the measurements. Each proposed simplification has a small test on which it can fail. Among them are the deepest four-point attachment, the integral middle zero mode before projection, the cubic response of a state with prescribed traces, and the cross term of two separated arithmetic bumps. Their power is that agreement on the data already used to define a candidate leaves the answer to each test undetermined.

    Research programme

    Quantum holography and associative chiral Koszul duality

    What boundary fields remember about collisions, line operators and the state of a bulk theory.

    Last updated 17 November 2026, 20:28 UTC · Contents

    Integrate out the interior of a disk while holding its boundary values fixed. Even for a free scalar, what survives depends on the question. The boundary current gives local products. A charged line changes the representation in which those products act. A path integral on the filling assigns amplitudes to the resulting states.

    Consider four charge-one lines at level two. A proper cluster has winding phase −1-1, and its coefficient extends cleanly. At the full collision, fixing even the dimensions of all stalks and costalks leaves a projective line of labelled perverse extensions. Requiring the fixed half-exchange +i+i and permutation symmetry leaves two of them. Requiring ordinary pullback from the coarse quotient selects one. Which condition the physical collision obeys is a question about its attachment at the diagonal.

    Associative chiral Koszul duality studies which operations survive when a field algebra is replaced by its bar construction. Ordered cuts, exchange of separated insertions and transverse composition of lines each supply structure. Quantum-group reconstruction needs coherent tensor products of the lines. Holographic reconstruction also asks how an independently defined bulk acts at the boundary and which filling prepares the measured state.
